卷三百二十 列傳第二百〇八 外國一 朝鮮

Volume 320 Biographies 208: Foreign States 1 - Korea

1
朝鮮，箕子所封國也。 漢以前曰朝鮮。 始為燕人衛滿所據，漢武帝平之，置真番、臨屯、樂浪、玄菟四郡。 漢末，有扶余人高氏據其地，改國號曰高麗，又曰高句麗，居平壤，即樂浪也。 已，為唐所破，東徙。 後唐時，王建代高氏，兼併新羅、百濟地，徙居松岳，曰東京，而以平壤為西京。 其國北鄰契丹，西則女直，南曰日本，元至元中，西京內屬，置東甯路總管府，盡慈嶺為界。
Korea was the state granted to Jizi as his fief. Before the Han dynasty it was known as Korea. It was first seized by Wei Man, a refugee from Yan, and when Emperor Wu of Han conquered the region he established the four commanderies of Zhenfan, Lintun, Lelang, and Xuantu. In the late Han, the Gao clan of the Fuyu people seized the region, renamed the state Goryeo—also known as Goguryeo—and made its capital at Pyongyang, formerly the seat of Lelang. Eventually Tang forces broke its power and it shifted eastward. Under Later Tang, Wang Jian overthrew the Gao line, absorbed Silla and Baekje, moved the capital to Songak as the Eastern Capital, and retained Pyongyang as the Western Capital. The kingdom bordered Khitan lands in the north, Jurchen territory to the west, and Japan to the south. In the Yuan reign-period Zhiyuan the Western Capital was brought under direct rule, an Eastern Ning Circuit chief commissioner's office was established, and Jichi Ridge marked the frontier.
2
明興，王高麗者王顓。 太祖即位之元年遣使賜璽書。 二年送還其國流人。 顓表賀，貢方物，且請封。 帝遣符璽郎偰斯齎詔及金印誥文封顓為高麗國王，賜曆及錦綺。 其秋，顓遣總部尚書成惟得、千牛衛大將軍金甲兩上表謝，並賀天壽節，因請祭服制度，帝命工部制賜之。 惟得等辭歸，帝從容問：「王居國何為？ 城郭修乎？ 兵甲利乎？ 宮室壯乎？ 」頓首言：「東海波臣，惟知崇信釋氏，他未遑也。 」遂以書諭之曰：「古者王公設險，未嘗去兵。 民以食為天，而國必有出政令之所。 今有人民而無城郭，人將何依？ 武備不修，則威弛； 地不耕，則民艱於食； 且有居室，無廳事，無以示尊嚴。 此數者朕甚不取。 夫國之大事，在祀與戎。 苟闕斯二者，而徒事佛求福，梁武之事，可為明鑒。 王國北接契丹、女直，而南接倭，備禦之道，王其念之。 」因賜之《六經》、《四書》、《通監》。 自是貢獻數至，元旦及聖節皆遣使朝賀，歲以為常。
When the Ming dynasty was founded, Goryeo was ruled by King Zhuan. In the first year of his reign the founding emperor sent envoys bearing an imperial letter under the imperial seal. In the second year the court returned exiles from Goryeo. Zhuan sent a memorial of congratulation with tribute goods and asked to receive formal investiture. The emperor dispatched the seal officer Qiesi with an investiture edict, a golden seal, and patent to enfeoff Zhuan as King of Goryeo, along with calendars and brocaded silks. That autumn Zhuan sent Cheng Weide, director-general of the central secretariat, and Jin Jialiang, general of the Thousand-Ox Guard, to submit memorials of thanks and to congratulate the emperor on his birthday, while also requesting specifications for sacrificial robes; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Works to make and grant them. When Weide and his party were about to depart, the emperor casually asked, "What does your king do to govern his realm? Are your fortifications kept in repair? Are your arms and armor in good order? Are your palaces suitably grand? They kowtowed and answered, "Your wave-tossed subject of the Eastern Sea knows only to revere Buddhism and has had no leisure for anything else. The emperor then wrote instructing him: "In antiquity lords fortified their domains and never dispensed with arms. The people regard food as their foundation, and every state needs a place from which to issue commands. If there are subjects but no walls, what will they rely upon? If military readiness is neglected, authority slackens. If the fields go untilled, the people will lack food. If there are dwellings but no hall of audience, there is no way to display royal dignity. In all these matters I strongly disapprove. The great affairs of state are sacrifice and war. To neglect both and seek blessings through Buddhism alone is a road whose end is visible in the example of Emperor Wu of Liang. Your realm borders the Khitan and Jurchen in the north and Wa in the south; consider well how you will defend it. He also granted copies of the Six Classics, the Four Books, and the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance. From then on tribute missions arrived frequently, and congratulatory envoys were sent every New Year and on the emperor's birthday as a standing practice.
3
三年正月命使往祀其國之山川。 是歲頒科舉詔於高麗，顓表謝，貢方物，並納元所授金印。 中書省言：「高麗貢使多齎私物入貨，宜徵稅； 又多攜中國物出境，禁之便。 」俱不許。 五年表請遣子弟入太學，帝曰：「入學固美事，但涉海遠，不欲者勿強。 」貢使洪師範、鄭夢周等一百五十餘人來京，失風溺死者三十九人，師範與焉。 帝憫之，遣元樞密使延安答裏往諭入貢毋數。 而顓復遣其門下贊成事姜仁裕來貢馬，其賀正旦使金湑等已先至，帝悉遣還。 謂中書省臣曰：「高麗貢獻繁數，既困敝其民，而涉海復虞覆溺。 宜遵古諸侯之禮，三年一聘。 貢物惟所產，毋過侈。 其明諭朕意。」
In the third year, during the first month, the court ordered envoys to perform sacrifices to the mountains and rivers of Goryeo. That year the civil service examination edict was promulgated in Goryeo; Zhuan sent a memorial of thanks with tribute goods and surrendered the golden seal the Yuan had conferred. The Central Secretariat reported, "Goryeo tribute envoys often bring private goods to sell and should be taxed accordingly. They also often carry goods from China out of the realm, and it would be best to forbid this. Both proposals were rejected. In the fifth year he memorialized asking to send sons and younger brothers to the Imperial Academy; the emperor said, "Study at court is a fine thing, but the sea voyage is long—do not force those who do not wish to go. More than 150 tribute envoys, including Hong Shifan and Zheng Mengzhou, came to the capital; thirty-nine drowned when their ships were lost in a storm, Shifan among them. The emperor took pity on them and sent the former privy council envoy Yanandali to instruct Goryeo not to send tribute so often. Yet Zhuan again sent his secretariat associate director Jiang Renyu to offer tribute horses, while his New Year congratulatory envoys, Jin Xu and others, had already arrived; the emperor sent them all back. He told the Central Secretariat ministers, "Goryeo's tribute missions are too frequent, exhausting its people, and the sea crossing again risks shipwreck and drowning. They should follow the rites of the ancient feudal lords and send envoys once every three years. Tribute goods should be limited to local products and not be excessive. Make my meaning clear to them."
4
六年，顓遣甲兩等貢馬五十匹，道亡其二，甲兩以聞。 及進，以私馬足之。 帝惡其不誠，卻之。 七年遣監門護軍周誼、鄭庇等來貢，表請每歲一貢，貢道從陸，由定遼，毋涉海，其貢物稱「送太府監」。 中書省言：「元時有太府監，本朝未嘗有，言涉不誠。 」帝命卻其貢。 是歲顓為權相李仁人所弑。 顓無子，以寵臣辛肫之子禑為子，於是仁人立禑。
In the sixth year Zhuan sent Jialiang and others to offer fifty horses in tribute; two were lost en route, and Jialiang reported the matter. When the tribute was presented, he made up the shortfall with his own horses. The emperor detested his lack of sincerity and refused the tribute. In the seventh year he sent gate guard army supervisor Zhou Yi, Zheng Bi, and others to offer tribute, memorializing to request annual tribute by land through Dingliao without crossing the sea, and describing the goods as "sent to the Directorate of Palace Provision." The Central Secretariat reported, "The Yuan had a Directorate of Palace Provision, but this dynasty has never had one—the wording suggests insincerity. The emperor ordered the tribute refused. That year Zhuan was assassinated by the powerful minister Li Renren. Zhuan had no son of his own and had adopted Bong, son of his favored minister Sin Chun; Renren thereupon enthroned Bong.
5
八年，禑遣判宗簿事崔原來告哀，且言前有貢使金義殺朝使蔡斌，今嗣王禑已誅義，籍其家。 帝疑其詐，拘原而遣使往祭吊。 十年，使來請故王顓諡號，帝曰：「顓被殺已久，今始請諡，將假吾朝命，鎮撫其民，且掩其弑逆之跡，不可許。 前所留使者，其遣之。 」於是釋原歸。 其夏，復遣周誼貢馬及方物，卻不受。 冬，又遣使賀明年正旦。 帝曰：「高麗王顓被弑，奸臣竊命，《春秋》之義，亂臣必誅，夫又何言。 第前後使者皆稱嗣王所遣，中書宜遣人往問嗣王如何，政令安在。 若政令如前，嗣王不為羈囚，則當依前王言，歲貢馬千匹，明年貢金百斤、銀萬兩、良馬百、細布萬，仍悉送還所拘遼東民，方見王位真而政令行，朕無惑已。 否則弑君之賊，必討無赦。」
In the eighth year Bong sent director of the register of the ancestral temple Cui Yuan to announce mourning, reporting that the former tribute envoy Jin Yi had killed the Ming envoy Cai Bin and that the succeeding king Bong had now executed Yi and confiscated his property. The emperor suspected deception, detained Yuan, and sent envoys to perform sacrificial rites of condolence. In the tenth year envoys came requesting a posthumous title for the former king Zhuan; the emperor said, "Zhuan was killed long ago, and they now ask for a posthumous title only to borrow our authority to pacify their people and cover the traces of regicide—it cannot be granted. Send back the envoys previously detained. Yuan was then released and sent home. That summer he again sent Zhou Yi with horses and local products, but the tribute was refused. In winter envoys were again sent to congratulate the New Year of the coming year. The emperor said, "King Zhuan of Goryeo was assassinated and treacherous ministers usurped power—in the sense of the Spring and Autumn Annals, rebellious ministers must be punished; what more is there to say? Yet envoys before and after all claim to have been sent by the succeeding king; the Central Secretariat should send someone to inquire into the succeeding king's condition and where governmental authority now lies. If governmental orders proceed as before and the succeeding king is not a captive, then according to the former king's words he should yearly offer a thousand horses, and next year offer a hundred catties of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, a hundred fine horses, and ten thousand bolts of fine cloth, while fully returning all Liaodong people detained—only then will it be clear that the kingship is genuine and orders are enforced, and I shall no longer be in doubt. Otherwise the regicides must be punished without pardon."
6
十一年四月，禑復命誼來貢。 十二年敕遼東守將潘敬、葉旺等謹飭邊備。 其冬，禑遣李茂芳等來貢，以不如約卻之。 十三年，遼東送高麗使誼至京師，帝敕敬等曰：「高麗弑君，又殺朝使，前堅請入貢又不如期，今遣誼來，以虛文飾詐，他日必為邊患。 自今來者，其絕勿通。 」因留誼于京師。 十六年來貢，卻之，命禮部責其朝貢過期、陪臣侮慢之罪； 誠欲聽約者，當以前五歲違約不貢之物並至。 十七年六月，禑遣司僕正崔涓、禮儀判書金進宜貢馬二千匹。 且言金非地所產，願以馬代輸，餘皆如約。 遼東守將唐勝宗為之請，帝許之。 然請顓諡號，襲王爵，未允也。
In the eleventh year, fourth month, Bong again ordered Yi to come with tribute. In the twelfth year the Liaodong frontier commanders Pan Jing, Ye Wang, and others were ordered to tighten border defenses. That winter Bong sent Li Maofang and others with tribute, but it was rejected because they had not fulfilled the agreement. In the thirteenth year Liaodong escorted the Goryeo envoy Yi to the capital; the emperor instructed Jing and others, "Goryeo's regicides also killed our envoys; they insisted on offering tribute yet again failed to meet the deadline—now sending Yi with empty words to gloss over deception, they will surely become a frontier threat. From now on, cut off all who come and do not admit them. Yi was therefore detained in the capital. In the sixteenth year they came with tribute and it was refused; the Ministry of Rites was ordered to charge them with overdue tribute and disrespect by accompanying ministers. If they truly wish to abide by the agreement, they must deliver together all goods owed from the previous five years of breached tribute. In the seventeenth year, sixth month, Bong sent master of the stud Cui Juan and director of ritual protocol Jin Jinyi to offer two thousand horses in tribute. They also reported that gold was not produced locally and asked to substitute horses in payment, with all else according to the agreement. The Liaodong frontier commander Tang Shengzhong pleaded on their behalf, and the emperor granted the request. However, the requests for Zhuan's posthumous title and succession to the kingship were not granted.
7
十八年正月，貢使至。 帝諭禮臣曰：「高麗屢請約束，朕數不允，而其請不已，故索歲貢以試其誠偽，非以此為富也。 今既聽命，宜損其貢數，令三年一朝，貢馬五十匹。 至二十一年正旦乃貢。 」七月，禑上表請襲爵，並請故王諡。 命封禑為高麗國王，賜故王顓諡恭湣。
In the eighteenth year, first month, the tribute envoys arrived. The emperor instructed the rites officials, "Goryeo has repeatedly requested binding agreements; I have several times refused, yet their requests never cease—therefore I demanded yearly tribute to test their sincerity, not to enrich myself. Now that they have obeyed, their tribute quota should be reduced: let them come once every three years and offer fifty horses. The next tribute should be offered at the New Year of the twenty-first year. In the seventh month Bong submitted a memorial requesting succession to the kingship and a posthumous title for the former king. Bong was enfeoffed as King of Goryeo, and the former king Zhuan was granted the posthumous title Gongmin.
8
十九年二月遣使貢布萬匹、馬千匹。 九月，表賀，貢方物。 其後貢獻輒逾常額，且未嘗至三年也。 冬，詔遣指揮僉事高家奴以綺布市馬於高麗。 二十年三月，高家奴還，陳高麗表辭馬直，帝敕如數償之。 先是，元末遼、瀋兵起，民避亂，轉徙高麗。 至是因市馬，帝令就索之，遂以遼、瀋流民三百餘口來歸。 十二月命戶部咨高麗王：「鐵嶺北，東西之地，舊屬開元者，遼東統之。 鐵嶺之南，舊屬高麗者，本國統之。 各正疆境，毋侵越。」
In the nineteenth year, second month, envoys were sent offering ten thousand bolts of cloth and a thousand horses. In the ninth month congratulatory memorials were sent with tribute goods. Thereafter tribute repeatedly exceeded the regular quota, and the three-year interval was never observed. In winter an edict dispatched assistant commander Gao Jianu to purchase horses in Goryeo with brocades and cloth. In the twentieth year, third month, Gao Jianu returned and reported Goryeo's memorial declining payment for the horses; the emperor ordered full payment according to the count. Earlier, when military disturbances arose in Liaoning and Shenyang at the end of the Yuan, people fleeing the turmoil migrated to Goryeo. On this occasion, because of the horse purchase, the emperor ordered them sought out there, and more than three hundred exiles from Liaoning and Shenyang returned. In the twelfth month the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to inform the King of Goryeo, "North of Tie Ridge, the lands east and west that formerly belonged to Kaiyuan shall be governed by Liaodong. South of Tie Ridge, what formerly belonged to Goryeo shall be governed by your state. Each side should rectify its borders and not encroach."
9
二十一年四月，禑表言，鐵嶺之地實其世守，乞仍舊便。 帝曰：「高麗舊以鴨綠江為界，今飾辭鐵嶺，詐偽昭然。 其以朕言諭之，俾安分，毋生釁端。 」八月，高麗千戶陳景來降，言：「是年四月，禑欲寇遼東，使都軍相崔瑩、李成桂繕兵西京。 成桂使陳景屯艾州，以糧不繼退師。 王怒，殺成桂之子。 成桂還兵攻破王城，囚王及瑩。 」景懼及，故降。 帝敕遼東嚴守備，仍遣人偵之。 十月，禑請遜位於其子昌。 帝曰：「前聞其王被囚，此必成桂之謀，姑俟之以觀變。」
In the twenty-first year, fourth month, Bong memorialized that the Tie Ridge region had in fact been held by his house for generations and asked that it remain as before. The emperor said, "Goryeo formerly took the Yalu River as its boundary; now dressing up words about Tie Ridge, its deception is manifest. Convey my words to them, that they keep to their place and not create incidents. In the eighth month the Goryeo chiliarch Chen Jing defected, reporting, "That year in the fourth month Bong intended to raid Liaodong and ordered commander-in-chief Cui Ying and Li Chenggui to ready troops at the Western Capital. Chenggui sent Chen Jing to garrison Aizhou, but because supplies failed the army withdrew. The king in anger killed Chenggui's son. Chenggui turned his army back, stormed the royal city, and imprisoned the king and Ying. Fearing he would be implicated, Chen surrendered. The emperor ordered Liaodong to tighten its defenses and sent men to reconnoiter. In the tenth month Bong requested to abdicate in favor of his son Chang. The emperor said, "We earlier heard that their king had been imprisoned—this must surely be Chenggui's doing; let us wait for now and see how affairs develop."
10
二十二年，權國事昌奏乞入朝，帝不許。 是歲，成桂廢昌，而立定昌國院君瑤。 二十三年正月遣使來告。 二十四年三月詔市馬高麗。 八月，權國事瑤進所市馬千五百匹。 帝曰； 「三韓君臣悖亂，二紀於茲。 今王瑤嗣立，乃王氏苗裔，宜遣使勞之。 」十二月，瑤遣其子奭朝賀明年正旦。 奭未歸而成桂自立，遂有其國，瑤出居原州。 王氏自五代傳國數百年，至是絕。
In the twenty-second year, regent Chang memorialized requesting an audience at court, but the emperor refused. That year Chenggui deposed Chang and installed Jeongchang Academy Lord Yao as ruler. In the twenty-third year, first month, envoys were sent to report the change. In the twenty-fourth year, third month, an edict ordered the purchase of horses in Goryeo. In the eighth month, regent Yao presented fifteen hundred horses purchased under the edict. The emperor said; "For two reign-periods now, the rulers and ministers of the Three Han have been in rebellion and disorder. King Yao has now succeeded to the throne; he is a descendant of the Wang house, and envoys should be sent to comfort him. "In the twelfth month Yao sent his son Suk to court to congratulate the New Year of the coming year. Before Suk returned, Chenggui declared himself ruler and took possession of the kingdom; Yao withdrew to Wonju. The Wang house had held the throne for several hundred years since the Five Dynasties period; with this it came to an end.
11
二十五年九月，高麗知密直司事趙胖等持國都評議司奏言：「本國自恭湣王薨，無嗣，權臣李仁人以辛肫子禑主國事，昏暴好殺，至欲興師犯邊，大將李成桂以為不可而回軍。 禑負罪惶懼，遜位於子昌。 國人弗順，啟請恭湣王妃安氏擇宗親瑤權國事。 已及四年，昏戾信讒，戕害勳舊，子奭癡騃不慧，國人謂瑤不足主社稷。 今以安氏命，退瑤於私第。 王氏子姓無可當輿望者，中外人心咸系成桂。 臣等與國人耆老共推主國事，惟聖主俞允。 」帝以高麗僻處東隅，非中國所治，令禮部移諭：「果能順天道，合人心，不啟邊釁，使命往來，實爾國之福，我又何誅。 」冬，成桂聞皇太子薨，遣使表慰，並請更國號。 帝命仍古號曰朝鮮。
In the twenty-fifth year, ninth month, Goryeo secret affairs director Zhao Pang and others presented a memorial from the state capital deliberative office, stating, "Since King Gongmin of our state died without an heir, the powerful minister Li Renren installed Sin Chun's son Bong to manage state affairs. He was tyrannical and bloodthirsty, even wishing to raise troops and violate the frontier; grand general Li Chenggui deemed this impossible and turned the army back. Burdened with guilt and fear, Bong abdicated in favor of his son Chang. The people would not accept this and petitioned Queen Consort An, widow of King Gongmin, to select the clansman Yao to manage state affairs. Four years had passed; he was muddled and perverse, believed slanders, and killed meritorious elders; his son Suk was dull and simple-minded, and the people deemed Yao unfit to rule the state. By Queen An's command Yao has now been retired to a private residence. Among the Wang clansmen there is none who can command public confidence; inside and outside the court, all hearts turn to Chenggui. We ministers, together with the elders of the state, jointly recommend him to manage state affairs, and ask that the sage sovereign graciously assent. The emperor, considering that Goryeo lay remote in the eastern corner and was not territory under China's direct governance, ordered the Ministry of Rites to transmit instructions: "If you can indeed follow Heaven's way, accord with the people's hearts, and not provoke border incidents, then the exchange of missions will truly be your state's blessing—why should I punish you? "In winter Chenggui, hearing that the crown prince had died, dispatched envoys with a memorial of condolence and also requested to change the state name. The emperor ordered that the ancient name Korea be retained.
12
二十六年二月遣使進馬九千八百餘匹，命運糸寧絲綿布一萬九千七百餘匹酬之。 六月表謝，貢馬及方物，並上前恭湣王金印，請更己名曰旦。 從之。 是月，遼東都指揮使司奏，朝鮮國招引女直五百餘人，潛渡鴨綠江，欲入寇。 乃遣使敕諭，示以禍福。 旦得敕，惶懼陳謝，上貢，並械送逋逃軍民三百八十餘人至遼東。
In the twenty-sixth year, second month, envoys were sent presenting more than nine thousand eight hundred horses; the court ordered more than nineteen thousand seven hundred bolts of silk, floss silk, and cotton cloth shipped in payment. In the sixth month a memorial of thanks was sent with tribute horses and local products, and the former King Gongmin's golden seal was surrendered; he requested to change his personal name to Dan. The request was granted. That month the Liaodong regional military commission reported that Korea had recruited more than five hundred Jurchen, secretly crossed the Yalu River, and intended to raid. Envoys were then dispatched with an imperial instruction, showing them the consequences of fortune and disaster. Dan received the instruction, and in fear and trepidation presented an apology, sent tribute, and also sent more than three hundred eighty deserting soldiers and civilians under guard to Liaodong.
13
二十七年，旦遣子入貢。 二十八年遣使柳珣賀明年正旦。 帝以表文語慢，詰責之。 珣言表文乃門下評理鄭道傳所撰，遂命逮道傳，釋珣歸。 二十九年送撰表人鄭總等三人至，雲表實總等所撰，道傳病不能行。 帝以總等亂邦構釁，留不遣。 三十年冬，復以表涉譏訕，拘其使。 建文初，旦表陳年老，以子芳遠襲位。 許之。
In the twenty-seventh year Dan sent his son to offer tribute. In the twenty-eighth year the envoy Liu Xun was dispatched to congratulate the New Year of the coming year. The emperor, finding the memorial's language disrespectful, reprimanded and censured him. Xun stated that the memorial had been composed by secretariat assessor Zheng Daotong; the court then ordered Daotong arrested and released Xun to return. In the twenty-ninth year they sent the memorial-drafters Zheng Zong and two others; they said the memorial had in fact been written by Zong and the others, and that Daotong was too ill to travel. The emperor, holding that Zong and the others had disordered the state and provoked border incidents, detained them and did not send them back. In the thirtieth year, winter, again because the memorial involved ridicule and satire, the envoy was detained. At the beginning of the Jianwen reign, Dan memorialized that he was advanced in years and had his son Bang-won (Fangyuan) succeed to the throne. Permission was granted.
14
成祖立，遣官頒即位詔。 永樂元年正月，芳遠遣使朝貢。 四月復遣陪臣李貴齡入貢，奏芳遠父有疾，需龍腦、沈香、蘇合、香油諸物，齎布求市。 帝命太醫院賜之，還其布。 芳遠表謝，因請冕服書藉。 帝嘉其能慕中國禮，賜金印、誥命、冕服、九章、圭玉、珮玉，妃珠翠七翟冠、霞帔、金墜，及經籍彩幣表裏。 自後貢獻，歲輒四五至焉。
When the Yongle Emperor established himself, officials were dispatched to promulgate the accession edict. In the first year of Yongle, first month, Bang-won dispatched envoys to pay court with tribute. In the fourth month he again sent attending minister Li Guiling to offer tribute, reporting that Bang-won's father was ill and needed dragon's brain, aloeswood, storax, sesame oil, and other items, and brought cloth to request purchase. The emperor ordered the Imperial Medical Academy to bestow them and returned his cloth. Bang-won sent a memorial of thanks and also requested court robes and books. The emperor commended his admiration for Chinese rites and granted a golden seal, patent of appointment, court robes, nine insignia, a jade scepter and pendant jade, for the consort a pearl-and-kingfisher seven-pheasant crown, embroidered cape, and gold pendants, as well as classics and brocades for outer and inner garments. Thereafter tribute missions came four or five times each year.
15
二年十二月詔立芳遠子禔為世子，從其請也。 五年十二月，貢馬三千匹至遼東，命戶部運絹布萬五千匹償之。 六年，世子禔來朝，賜織金文綺。 及歸，帝親制詩賜之。 時朝鮮納女後宮，立為妃嬪者四人。 其秋，遣陪臣鄭擢來告其父旦之喪。 命官弔祭，賜諡康獻。
In the second year, twelfth month, an edict established Bang-won's son Je as heir apparent, acceding to his request. In the fifth year, twelfth month, three thousand tribute horses arrived at Liaodong; the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to transport ten thousand five hundred bolts of silk cloth in payment. In the sixth year heir apparent Je came to court and was granted gold-woven brocades. When he returned, the emperor personally composed a poem and bestowed it on him. At that time Korea offered women to the inner palace, and four were established as consorts and concubines. That autumn he sent attending minister Zheng Zhuo to report the death of his father Dan. Officials were ordered to offer condolences and sacrifices, and the posthumous title Kangxian was granted.
16
十六年奏世子禔不肖，第三子祹孝弟力學，國人所屬，請立為嗣，詔聽王所擇。 因上表謝，並陳己年老，請以祹理國事。 命光祿少卿韓確、鴻臚丞劉泉封祹為朝鮮國王。 時帝已遷北都，朝鮮益近，而事大之禮益恭，朝廷亦待以加禮，他國不敢望也。
In the sixteenth year he memorialized that heir apparent Je was unworthy, while the third son Do was filial, fraternal, and diligent in learning—the people looked to him—and requested that he be established as successor; an edict granted the king his choice. He then presented a memorial of thanks and also stated that he was advanced in years, requesting that Do manage state affairs. Vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Han Que and Honglu secretariat assistant Liu Quan were ordered to invest Do as King of Korea. By then the emperor had already moved the capital north; Korea was all the nearer, and its rites of serving the great power grew ever more deferential—the court also treated it with added ceremony, which other states did not dare expect.
17
二十年，芳遠卒，賜諡恭定。 二十一年七月，祹請立嫡子珦為世子，從之。 先是，敕祹貢馬萬匹，至是如數至，賜白金綺絹。
In the twentieth year Bang-won died, and the posthumous title Gongding was granted. In the twenty-first year, seventh month, Do requested to establish his eldest son Gyeong as heir apparent, and the request was granted. Earlier an instruction had ordered Do to offer ten thousand horses in tribute; by this time the full number had arrived, and white silver and brocade silk were granted.
18
宣德二年三月遣中官賜白金糸寧紗，別敕進馬五千匹，資邊用。 九月如數至。 四年祹賜書：「珍禽異獸，非朕所貴，其勿獻。 」後又敕祹：「金玉之器，非爾國所產，宜止之，土物效誠而已。 」八年，祹奏遣子弟詣太學或遼東學，帝不許，賜《五經》、《四書》、《性理》、《通鑒綱目》諸書。
In the third year of Xuande, third month, palace eunuchs were dispatched to grant white silver and silk gauze; a separate instruction ordered the presentation of five thousand horses to supply the border. In the ninth month the full number arrived. In the fourth year Do was granted a letter: "Rare birds and exotic beasts are not what I value—do not present them. "Later another instruction to Do: "Vessels of gold and jade are not products of your state—you should cease presenting them; local goods to show sincerity are enough. "In the eighth year Do memorialized requesting to send sons and younger brothers to the Imperial Academy or the Liaodong Academy; the emperor did not permit it but granted the Five Classics, Four Books, Xingli, Zizhi Tongjian Gangmu, and other books.
19
正統元年三月放朝鮮婦女金黑等五十三人還其國。 金黑等自宣德初至京師，至是遣中官送回。 三年八月賜祹遠遊冠、絳紗袍、玉佩、赤舄。 先是，建州長童倉避居朝鮮界，已復還建州。 朝鮮言：「昔以窮歸臣，臣遇之善。 今負恩還建州李滿住所，慮其同謀擾邊。 」建州長言，所部為朝鮮追殺，阻留一百七十餘家。 五年詔祹還之。 七年五月諭祹曰：「鴨綠江一帶東甯等衛，密邇王境，中多細人逃至王國，或被國人誘脅去者，無問漢人、女直，至即解京。 」初，瓦剌密令女直諸部誘朝鮮，使背中國。 祹拒之，白其事於朝。 帝嘉其忠，敕獎之，並賜彩幣。 九年春，倭寇犯邊，祹命將擒獲五十餘人，械送京師。 十年又獲餘黨來獻。 帝連敕獎諭，賜賚加等。 十三年冬，命使調發朝鮮及野人女直兵會遼東，征北寇。 時英宗北狩，郕王即位，遣官頒詔于其國。
In the first year of Zhengtong, third month, fifty-three Korean women including Jin Hei were released and sent back to their state. Jin Hei and the others had come to the capital since the beginning of Xuande; on this occasion palace eunuchs were dispatched to escort them back. In the third year, eighth month, Do was granted the distant-travel crown, crimson gauze robe, jade pendant, and red slippers. Earlier, Jianzhou chieftain Tongcang had taken refuge within Korea's border and had already returned to Jianzhou. Korea stated, "Formerly he came in destitution to submit to us, and we treated him well. Now, ungratefully, he has returned to Li Manju's place in Jianzhou, and we fear they will conspire together to disturb the border. "The Jianzhou chieftain stated that his followers had been pursued and killed by Korea, and more than one hundred seventy households were blocked and detained. In the fifth year an edict ordered Do to return them. In the seventh year, fifth month, Do was instructed, "Along the Yalu River the guards such as Eastern Ning closely border your realm; among them many common folk flee to your kingdom, or are lured and coerced away by your people—regardless of whether Han Chinese or Jurchen, when they arrive send them immediately to the capital. "Earlier the Oirats secretly ordered the Jurchen tribes to entice Korea, making it turn against China. Do refused them and reported the matter to the court. The emperor commended his loyalty, issued an instruction praising him, and also granted colored silks. In the ninth year, spring, Wa pirates violated the border; Do ordered his generals to capture more than fifty men and sent them in bonds to the capital. In the tenth year the remaining band was again captured and presented. The emperor repeatedly issued instructions praising and instructing him, with enhanced gifts. In the thirteenth year, winter, envoys were ordered to mobilize Korean and wild Jurchen troops to assemble at Liaodong and campaign against the northern raiders. At that time Emperor Yingzong was on the northern hunt; the Prince of Cheng established himself and dispatched officials to promulgate an edict in that state.
20
景泰元年貢馬五百匹。 奏稱奉敕辦馬二三萬匹，比因鄰寇構釁，馬畜踣斃，一時未能。 詔曰：「寇今少息。 馬已至者，償其直。 未至者，止勿貢。 」是年夏，祹卒，賜弔祭，諡莊憲，封子珦為國王。 會遼東奏報開原、瀋陽有寇入境，掠人畜，系建州、海西、野人女直頭目李滿住等為嚮導，因諭珦相為掎角截殺之。 其秋，續貢馬千五百餘匹。 賜冕服，並償其直。 冬又賜珦及妃權氏誥命，封其子弘為世子。 二年冬，以建州頭目潛與朝鮮通，戒珦絕其使。 三年秋，珦卒，來告哀。 遣中官往弔祭，賜諡恭順，命子弘嗣立。 弘立三年，以年幼且嬰夙疾，請以叔瑈權國事。 七年上表遜位，乃封瑈為國王。 瑈請立子暲為世子，從之。
In the first year of Jingtai, five hundred tribute horses were offered. The memorial stated that by imperial instruction they were to supply twenty or thirty thousand horses; recently, because neighboring raiders had provoked incidents, horses and livestock had fallen and died, and they could not do so for the moment. An edict said, "The raiders have now somewhat subsided. For horses already arrived, pay their price. For those not yet arrived, cease—do not offer tribute. "That summer Do died; condolences and sacrifices were granted, the posthumous title Zhuangxian was bestowed, and his son Gyeong was invested as king. Just then Liaodong reported that raiders had entered Kaiyuan and Shenyang, looting people and livestock, with Jianzhou, Haixi, and wild Jurchen chieftains Li Manju and others serving as guides; Gyeong was therefore instructed to cooperate in pincer attacks to intercept and destroy them. That autumn more than fifteen hundred additional tribute horses were offered. Court robes were granted and payment was made for the horses. In winter patents of appointment were again granted to Gyeong and his consort Lady Quan, investing his son Hong-wi as heir apparent. In the second year, winter, because Jianzhou chieftains had secretly communicated with Korea, Gyeong was warned to cut off relations with them. In the third year, autumn, Gyeong died, and envoys came to report mourning. Palace eunuchs were dispatched to offer condolences and sacrifices; the posthumous title Gongshun was granted, and his son Hong-wi was ordered to succeed. Hong-wi had reigned three years; being young and afflicted with chronic illness since infancy, he requested that his uncle Yu manage state affairs. In the seventh year he presented a memorial abdicating, and Yu was thereupon invested as king. Yu requested to establish his son Yeong as heir apparent, and the request was granted.
21
天順三年，邊將奏，有建州三衛都督私與朝鮮結，恐為中國患。 因敕瑈毋作不靖，貽後悔。 瑈疏辨，復諭曰：「宣德、正統年間，以王國與彼互相侵掠，敕解怨息兵，初不令交通給賞授官也。 彼既受朝廷官職，王又加之，是與朝廷抗也。 王素秉禮義，何爾文過飾非？ 後宜絕私交，以全令譽。 」四年復諭瑈曰：「王奏毛憐衛都督郎卜兒哈通謀煽亂，已置之法。 夫法止可行于國中，豈得加於鄰境。 郎卜兒哈有罪，宜奏朝廷區處。 今輒行殺害，何怪其子阿比車之思復仇也。 聞阿比車之母尚在，宜急送遼東都司，令阿比車領回，以解仇怨。 」五年，建州衛野人至義州殺掠，瑈奏乞朝命還所掠。 兵部議：「朝鮮先嘗誘殺郎卜兒哈，繼又誘致都指揮兀克，縱兵掠其家屬。 今野人實系復仇，宜諭朝鮮，寇盜之來皆自取，惟守分安法，庶弭邊釁。 」從之。
In the third year of Tianshun, border generals reported that commanders of the three Jianzhou guards had privately allied with Korea, fearing this would become a calamity for China. Yu was thereupon instructed not to act unruly, lest he bring later regret. Yu submitted a memorial in defense; he was again instructed, "During the Xuande and Zhengtong reigns, because your kingdom and they mutually raided one another, an instruction was issued to resolve enmity and cease arms—it did not permit communication, granting rewards, or conferring office. Since they have already received offices from the court, and the king adds to them, this is opposing the court. You have always upheld ritual and righteousness—why do you now gloss over your faults and conceal your wrongs? Henceforth you should sever private ties, so as to preserve your good reputation." In the fourth year Yu was again instructed: "You memorialized that Maolin Guard Commander Langbu'erha conspired to incite rebellion, and he has been executed according to law. Law may be applied only within one's own state—how can it be imposed on neighboring territory? If Langbu'erha had committed a crime, you should have memorialized the court to handle the matter. Now you rashly carried out the killing—no wonder his son Abiche seeks revenge. We hear that Abiche's mother is still alive. You should promptly send her to the Liaodong regional command and let Abiche take her back, so as to resolve the feud." In the fifth year Jianzhou wild Jurchen raided Yizhou, killing and plundering. Yu memorialized, requesting a court order for the return of plundered goods. The Ministry of War deliberated: "Korea first lured Langbu'erha to his death, then lured Battalion Commander Wuke and unleashed troops to plunder his household. The wild Jurchen are in fact seeking revenge. Korea should be told that these raids are of its own making, and that only by keeping within its bounds and observing the law can border troubles be quelled." This was approved.
22
成化元年冬，陪臣李門炯來朝，卒於道。 命給棺賜祭，並賜彩幣慰其家。 時朝鮮頻貢異物，三年春，敕諭瑈修常貢，勿事珍奇。 是時朝廷用兵征建州，敕瑈助兵進剿。 瑈遣中樞府知事康純統眾萬餘渡鴨綠、潑豬二江，攻破九獮府諸寨，斬獲多。
In the winter of the first year of Chenghua, the Korean envoy Li Menjiong came to court but died en route. He was granted a coffin and sacrificial offerings, and colored silks were also bestowed to comfort his family. Korea was then frequently sending exotic tribute items. In the spring of the third year an instruction admonished Yu to keep to regular tribute and not indulge in rare curiosities. At this time the court was campaigning against Jianzhou and instructed Yu to assist the troops in the punitive advance. Yu sent Kang Chun, Director of the Secretariat, at the head of more than ten thousand men across the Yalu and Pozhu Rivers. They stormed the stockades of Jiun Prefecture and took many heads and captives.
23
四年正月遣官來獻俘。 詔從厚賚，敕獎諭之。 是年，瑈卒，賜諡惠莊。 遣太監鄭同、崔安封世子晄為王，給妃韓氏誥命。 既行，巡按遼東御史侯英奏曰：「遼東連年被寇，瘡痍未起，今復禾稼不登，軍民乏食。 太監鄭同等隨從人員所過驛騷。 臣考先年曾于翰林院中，選有學行文望者出使。 今同、安俱朝鮮人，墳墓宗族皆在，見其國王，不免屈節，殊褻中國體。 乞寢成命，或翰林，或給事中及行人內推選一員，往使為便。 」帝曰：「英所言良是。 自後賞賚遣內臣，其冊封正副使，選廷臣有學行者。」
In the first month of the fourth year envoys were sent to present captives. An edict granted generous rewards, and an instruction praised and commended them. That year Yu died and was granted the posthumous title Huizhuang. The eunuchs Zheng Tong and Cui An were dispatched to invest heir apparent Gwang as king, and patent of appointment was granted to his consort Lady Han. After they had set out, Hou Ying, the touring censor of Liaodong, memorialized: "Liaodong has been raided year after year; it has not yet recovered from the devastation, crops have again failed, and soldiers and civilians alike lack food. Wherever the eunuchs Zheng Tong and the others passed with their retinues, they disturbed the relay stations. Your subject notes that in former years men of learning, literary attainment, and standing were selected from the Hanlin Academy to serve as envoys abroad. Zheng Tong and Cui An are both Koreans; their ancestral graves and clans are all there. In audience with the Korean king they cannot but demean themselves—grievously compromising the dignity of the empire. I beg that the present appointment be revoked and that one be selected instead from the Hanlin Academy, the supervising secretaries, or the heralds—this would be far more appropriate for such a mission." The emperor said: "What Hou Ying said is quite correct. Henceforth palace eunuchs may be sent to convey rewards, but chief and deputy investiture envoys shall be chosen from among court officials of learning and good conduct."
24
六年，晄病篤，以所生子幼，命其兄故世子暲女子娎子權國事，遣陪臣以聞。 及卒，賜諡襄悼，命娎嗣位，娎妻韓氏封王妃。 十年追贈娎父世子暲為國王，諡懷簡，母韓氏為王妃，從所請也。
In the sixth year Gwang fell gravely ill. Because his own son was still young, he placed state affairs in the hands of Hyeon, son of his elder brother the late heir apparent Yeong's daughter, and sent envoys to report this to the court. When he died he was granted the posthumous title Xiangdao. Hyeon was ordered to succeed him, and Hyeon's wife Lady Han was invested as queen consort. In the tenth year Hyeon's father, heir apparent Yeong, was posthumously enfeoffed as king and granted the posthumous title Huaijian; his mother Lady Han was posthumously invested as queen consort, as requested.
25
十一年四月，娎奏建州野人糾聚毛憐等衛侵擾邊境不已，乞朝命戒飭。 十二年十月，娎為繼妻尹氏請封，賜誥命冠服。 時禁外國互市兵器，娎奏：「小邦北連野人，南鄰倭島，五兵之用，不可缺一。 而弓材所需牛角，仰于上國。 高皇帝時嘗賜火藥、火砲，今望特許收買弓角，不與外番同禁。 」兵部議歲市弓角五十，後以不足於用，請無限額，詔許倍市。
In the fourth month of the eleventh year Hyeon memorialized that Jianzhou wild Jurchen had gathered with Maolin and other guards to harass the border incessantly, and requested a court order for their restraint. In the tenth month of the twelfth year Hyeon requested investiture for his second wife, Lady Yun; patent of appointment along with cap and robes were granted. Foreign states were then forbidden from trading in weapons. Hyeon memorialized: "Our small state borders wild Jurchen to the north and the Wa islands to the south. We cannot do without any of the five weapons of war. Yet the ox horns needed for bow-making depend entirely on the superior state. In the time of the August Emperor gunpowder and cannon were once granted to us. We now hope for special permission to purchase bow horns, and not to be subject to the same prohibition as other foreign peoples." The Ministry of War fixed an annual purchase of fifty bow horns. When this proved insufficient, an unlimited quota was requested, and an edict permitted purchasing at double the original amount.
26
十五年十月命娎出兵夾擊建州女直。 娎遂遣右贊成魚有沼率兵至滿浦江，以水泮後期。 復遣左議政尹弼商、節度使金嶠等渡江進剿。 十六年春遣陪臣來獻捷，帝命內官齎敕獎其能繼先烈，賜金幣，領兵官賞賚如例。 後使還，遣其臣許熙伴送。 熙歸至開州，建州騎二千邀之，掠其從卒三十余人，馬二百三十餘匹，他所亡物稱是。 奏聞，英國公張懋、吏部尚書尹旻等以遼東連年用兵，未可輕動，宜以此意諭娎。 敕遼東守臣整飭邊備，更令譯者窮究所掠，期在必得，仍賜熙白金彩幣慰安之。
In the tenth month of the fifteenth year Hyeon was ordered to dispatch troops for a pincer attack against the Jianzhou Jurchen. Hyeon then sent Yu Yozhao, Right Chancery Councillor, with troops to the Manpu River, but they arrived late because the ice had melted. He then sent Left State Councillor Yin Bishang, Military Commissioner Jin Qiao, and others across the river to advance in suppression. In the spring of the sixteenth year envoys were sent to report victory. The emperor ordered palace officials to convey an instruction commending their ability to carry on their forefathers' achievements, granted gold and silks, and rewarded the commanding officers according to precedent. When the envoys later returned, Hyeon dispatched his minister Xu Xi to escort the imperial messenger. When Xu Xi reached Kaichou on his return, two thousand Jianzhou horsemen waylaid him, plundering more than thirty of his attendants, over two hundred thirty horses, and a comparable quantity of other goods. On receiving the report, the Duke of Ying Zhang Mao, Minister of Personnel Yin Min, and others held that because Liaodong had seen warfare year after year and could not be lightly disturbed, this sentiment should be conveyed to Hyeon. An instruction ordered Liaodong officials to strengthen border defenses, and further ordered interpreters to pursue a thorough investigation of the plunder with every expectation of recovery. Xu Xi was also granted white gold and colored silks by way of consolation.
27
十七年，娎奏繼妃尹氏失德，廢置，乞更封副室尹氏。 從之。 十九年四月封娎長子㦕為世子。
In the seventeenth year Hyeon memorialized that his second consort Lady Yun had proved devoid of virtue and been deposed, and requested that his secondary consort Lady Yun be invested in her stead. This was granted. In the fourth month of the nineteenth year Hyeon's eldest son Yeon was invested as heir apparent.
28
弘治七年十二月，娎卒，賜諡康靖。 明年四月，封㦕為國，妻慎氏為王妃。 十二年，㦕奏：「本國人屢有違禁匿海島，誘引軍民，漸至滋蔓。 乞許本國自行搜刷。 其系上國地方，請敕官追捕。 」時遼東守臣亦奏如㦕言，報可。 十五年冬，封㦕長子為世子。
In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Hongzhi Hyeon died and was granted the posthumous title Kangjing. In the fourth month of the following year Yeon was invested as king, and his wife Lady Shen was invested as queen consort. In the twelfth year Yeon memorialized: "Our people have repeatedly violated the prohibitions by hiding on sea islands and luring away soldiers and civilians, and the problem has gradually spread. We beg permission for our state to conduct searches and purges on its own. As for those found in territory of the superior state, we request that officials be instructed to pursue and capture them." The Liaodong garrison officials also memorialized to the same effect as Yeon, and this was approved. In the winter of the fifteenth year Yeon's eldest son was invested as heir apparent.
29
正德二年，㦕以世子夭亡，哀慟成疾，奏請以國事付其弟懌，其國人復奏請封懌。 禮部議命懌權理國事，俟㦕卒乃封。 既，陪臣盧公弼等以朝貢至京，復請封懌，廷議不允。 十二月，㦕母妃奏懌長且賢，堪付重寄。 於是禮部奏：「㦕以痼疾辭位，懌以親弟承托，接受既明，友愛不失。 通國臣民舉無異詞，宜順其請。 」上乃允懌嗣位，遣中官敕封，並賜其妃尹氏誥命。 初，成桂之自立也，與宰相李仁人本異族。 永樂間，降祭海岳祝文，稱成桂為仁人子，而《祖訓》亦載仁人子成桂更名旦。 後成桂子芳遠奏辨，太宗許令改正。 至是修《大明會典》，仍列《祖訓》于朝鮮國。 貢使市以歸，懌上疏備陳世系，辨先世無弑逆事，乞改正。 禮部議：「《會典》詳載本朝制度，事涉外國，疑似之際，在所略。 況成桂得國出皇祖命，其不系仁人後，太宗詔可征，宜從其請。 」詔曰：「可。」
In the second year of Zhengde, when the heir apparent died young, Yeon grieved himself into illness and memorialized requesting that state affairs be entrusted to his younger brother Eul; his subjects also memorialized requesting that Eul be invested. The Ministry of Rites deliberated that Eul should be ordered to manage state affairs provisionally, with formal investiture to follow only after Yeon's death. Later, when the envoys Lu Gongbi and others arrived at the capital on tribute, they again requested that Eul be invested, but court deliberation did not consent. In the twelfth month Yeon's queen mother memorialized that Eul was older and worthy, and fit to be entrusted with grave responsibility. Thereupon the Ministry of Rites memorialized: "Yeon, owing to chronic illness, has abdicated; Eul, as his younger brother, has accepted the trust. The transfer of authority is clear and brotherly affection remains intact. Throughout the kingdom officials and people are unanimously agreed; their request should be granted." The emperor then permitted Eul to succeed. Palace eunuchs were dispatched with an instruction to invest him, and patent of appointment was also granted to his consort Lady Yun. Earlier, when Seong Gye established himself in power, he and Chancellor Li Renren had originally been of different clans. During the Yongle reign, when sacrificial texts to the mountains and seas were issued, Seong Gye was called the son of Renren, and the Ancestral Admonitions also records "Renren's son Seong Gye, renamed Dan." Later Seong Gye's son Bang-won memorialized in defense, and the Taizong Emperor permitted the record to be corrected. At this time, while revising the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming, the Ancestral Admonitions was still listed under the Korean state. A tribute envoy purchased a copy and returned with it. Eul submitted a memorial fully setting forth his dynastic line, arguing that his forebears had never committed regicide, and begged that the record be corrected. The Ministry of Rites deliberated: "The Collected Statutes fully records this dynasty's institutions; where matters involve foreign states and points remain doubtful, they are to be omitted. Moreover, Seong Gye's obtaining the throne issued from the imperial ancestor's command, and that he was not of Renren's line was confirmed by the Taizong Emperor's edict. Their request should be granted." An edict said: "Permitted."
30
十五年冬，命內官封懌子峼為世子，賜懌金帛珠玉，令括取異物及童男女以進。 十六年，世宗即位，禮官言：「天子初踐祚，宜正中國之體，絕外裔狎侮之端。 請諭懌非朝廷意，召內臣還，毋有所索取。 」帝從之。
In the winter of the fifteenth year palace eunuchs were ordered to invest Eul's son Jeong as heir apparent. Eul was granted gold, silks, pearls, and jade, and ordered to gather exotic goods and boys and girls to present as tribute. In the sixteenth year the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne. The ritual officials said: "When the Son of Heaven first ascends the throne, the dignity of the Central State should be set right and the beginnings of foreign presumption cut off. We request that Eul be told this was not the court's intent, that the palace eunuchs be recalled, and that nothing further be demanded." The emperor approved this.
31
嘉靖二年八月，以俘獲倭夷來獻，並送還中國被掠八人。 賜白金錦糸寧。
In the eighth month of the second year of Jiajing, captives of Wa barbarians were presented, and eight Chinese subjects who had been seized were also returned. White gold and brocade silks were granted in reward.
32
八年八月，陪臣柳溥上言：國祖李旦系本國全州人。 二十八世祖瀚仕新羅為司空。 新羅亡，六世孫兢休入高麗。 十三世孫安社仕元為南京千戶所達魯花赤。 元季兵興，安曾孫子春與男成桂避地東遷。 至正辛丑，當恭湣王之十年，有紅巾賊入境，成桂擊賊有功，授武班職事，時尚未知名。 恭湣無嗣，陰蓄寵臣辛肫之子禑為子，晚為嬖臣洪倫、內豎崔萬生所弑。 權臣李仁人誅倫、萬生而立禑，擢成桂為門下侍中。 禑遣成桂侵遼東，成桂不從，返兵。 禑懼，遜位於子昌。 昌以偽姓見黜，復立王氏裔定昌君瑤，竄仁人於外。 瑤復不道，國人戴成桂，請于高皇帝，立為王，更名旦，贍瑤別邸，終其身，實未嘗為弑。 前永樂、正德間屢經奏請，俱蒙俞允，而迄未改正。 今遇重修《會典》，乞賜昭雪。 」詔送史館編纂。
In the eighth month of the eighth year the envoy Liu Pu stated: "Our dynastic founder Li Dan was a native of Jeonju in our state. Our twenty-eighth-generation ancestor Han served Silla as Minister of Works. When Silla perished, the sixth-generation descendant Gyeong-hyu entered Goryeo. The thirteenth-generation descendant An-sa served the Yuan as darughachi of the Nanjing Thousand-Household Guard. When warfare arose in the late Yuan, An-sa's great-great-grandson Ja-chun and his son Seong Gye moved east to escape the turmoil. In xinchou of the Zhizheng era, the tenth year of King Gongmin, Red Turban bandits entered the territory. Seong Gye struck the bandits with merit and was appointed to a military office, though he was not yet widely known. Gongmin had no heir. He secretly adopted Sin Don's son Ui as his own, and in his later years was assassinated by the favorite Hong Lun and the palace attendant Cui Man-saeng. The powerful minister Li Renren executed Lun and Man-saeng and established Ui on the throne, promoting Seong Gye to Palace Attendant-in-Waiting. Ui sent Seong Gye to invade Liaodong, but Seong Gye refused and turned the army back. Ui, in fear, abdicated in favor of his son Chang. Chang was dismissed for using a false surname. The Wang-clan descendant Prince Jeongchang Yao was restored to the throne, and Renren was banished abroad. Yao again proved unprincipled. The people upheld Seong Gye, petitioned the August Emperor, and established him as king, renaming him Dan. Yao was housed in a separate residence for life—he was in fact never murdered. Previously, during the Yongle and Zhengde reigns, memorials had repeatedly been submitted and all had received approval, yet the record had never been corrected. Now, as the Collected Statutes are being revised, we beg that exoneration be granted." An edict ordered the matter sent to the Historiography Institute for compilation.
33
十八年二月，睿宗祔太廟，配享明堂禮成，懌表賀。 帝特禦奉天門引見，賜宴禮部。
In the second month of the eighteenth year, when the rites were completed for enshrining the Ruizong Emperor in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and associating him in worship at the Bright Hall, Eul submitted a congratulatory memorial. The emperor specially proceeded to the Gate of Receiving Heaven to grant him audience and bestowed a banquet at the Ministry of Rites.
34
二十三年冬，懌卒。 二十四年正月來訃，賜諡恭僖。 詔立其子峼。 峼未逾年卒，賜諡榮靖。 九月，峼弟權國事峘遣使謝祭諡，並請襲封，詔許之。
In the winter of the twenty-third year Eul died. In the first month of the twenty-fourth year mourning was reported, and the posthumous title Gongxi was granted. An edict established his son Jeong as king. Jeong died within the year and was granted the posthumous title Rongjing. In the ninth month Jeong's younger brother Sun, who was managing state affairs, dispatched envoys to thank the court for the sacrificial offerings and posthumous title and to request succession by investiture; an edict permitted this.
35
二十五年，峘遣使送下海番人六百余至邊，賜金幣。 二十六年正月，峘咨稱：「福建人從無泛海至本國者，因往日本市易，為風所漂，前後共獲千人以上，皆挾軍器貨物，致中國火砲亦為倭有，恐起兵端。 」詔：「頃年沿海奸民犯禁，福建尤甚，往往為外國所獲，有傷國體。 海道官員令巡按御史察參。 仍賜王銀幣，以旌其忠。」
In the twenty-fifth year Sun dispatched envoys to send more than six hundred overseas barbarians to the border, and gold and silks were granted in reward. In the first month of the twenty-sixth year Sun reported: "Never before had people from Fujian sailed the seas to our state. Having gone to trade in Japan, they were blown off course by wind; more than a thousand were captured in all, all carrying weapons and goods, so that Chinese cannon also fell into Wa hands—we fear this may spark war. An edict said: "In recent years wicked people along the coast have violated the prohibitions, Fujian especially. They have often been seized by foreign states, to the harm of national dignity. Officials responsible for maritime routes were ordered to be investigated and impeached by touring censors. Silver and silks were still granted to the king in recognition of his loyalty."
36
三十一年冬，以洪武、永樂間所賜樂器敝壞，奏求律管，更乞遣樂官赴京校習，許之。
In the winter of the thirty-first year, because the musical instruments granted during the Hongwu and Yongle reigns had fallen into disrepair, a memorial requested new pitch-pipes and asked that musicians be sent to the capital for training; the request was granted.
37
三十五年五月有倭船四自浙、直敗還，漂入朝鮮境。 峘遣兵擊殲之，得中國被俘及助逆者三十餘人來獻，因賀冬至節，帝賜璽書褒諭。 三十八年十一月奏：「今年五月，有倭寇駕船二十五隻來抵海岸，臣命將李鐸等剿殺殆盡，獲中國民陳春等三百餘人，內招通倭嚮導陳得等十六人，俱獻闕下。 」復降敕獎勵，厚賚銀幣，並賜鐸等有差。
In the fifth month of the thirty-fifth year four Japanese ships, beaten while returning from Zhejiang and Zhili, were driven by wind and tide into Korean waters. Sun dispatched troops to attack and annihilate them, recovered more than thirty captured Chinese and renegades who had aided the enemy, and sent them to the court as tribute. On the occasion of his congratulations for the Winter Solstice, the emperor rewarded him with an imperial sealed letter of praise. In the eleventh month of the thirty-eighth year a memorial stated: "This year in the fifth month twenty-five Wa pirate ships reached the coast. Your subject ordered Generals Li T'o and others to exterminate nearly all of them, recovering more than three hundred Chinese civilians including Chen Chun. Among them were sixteen who had colluded with the Wa as guides, including Chen De—all were sent to the court. " An edict was again issued commending and rewarding them, generously granting silver and silks, and T'o and the others were rewarded according to rank.
38
四十二年九月，峘復上書辨先世非李仁人後，今修《會典》雖蒙厘正，乞著始祖旦、父子春之名，帝令附錄《會典》。
In the ninth month of the forty-second year Sun again submitted a memorial clarifying that his forebears were not descendants of Li Renren. Although the revised Collected Statutes of the Ming Dynasty had been corrected on this point, he begged that the names of the founding ancestor Dan and his son Zichun be formally recorded; the emperor ordered them appended to the Collected Statutes.
39
隆慶元年六月遣官頒即位詔。 時帝將幸太學，來使乞留觀禮，許之。 是年冬，峘卒，賜諡恭憲，命其侄昖襲封。
In the sixth month of the first year of Longqing officials were dispatched to proclaim the accession edict. At that time the emperor was about to visit the Imperial Academy; the envoy requested permission to remain and observe the ceremony, and this was granted. That winter Sun died and was granted the posthumous title Gongxian; his nephew Seon was ordered to succeed to the kingship.
40
萬曆元年正月上穆宗尊諡、兩宮徽號禮成，昖表賀，獻方物馬匹。 時昖屢請賜《皇明會典》，為其先康獻王旦雪冤。 十六年正月，《會典》成，適貢使愈泓在京，請給前書，以終前命。 許之。 十七年十一月，陪臣奇芩等入賀冬至，奏稱本年六月，大琉球國船遭風至海岸，所有男婦合解京，給文放歸。 從之。
In the first month of the first year of Wanli, when the rites were completed for bestowing the posthumous title upon the Muzong Emperor and the honorific titles upon the two palaces, Seon submitted a congratulatory memorial and presented local products and horses. At that time Seon repeatedly requested a copy of the Collected Statutes of the Ming Dynasty to vindicate his forebear King Kangxian Dan. In the first month of the sixteenth year the Collected Statutes were completed; the tribute envoy Yu Hong happened to be in the capital and requested the book previously promised, to fulfill the earlier command. Permission was granted. In the eleventh month of the seventeenth year the attendant minister Gi Eun and others came to congratulate on the Winter Solstice and reported that in the sixth month of that year a ship from Great Ryukyu had been blown by wind to the coast; all the men and women aboard should be sent together to the capital and then released with travel documents. Approval was granted.
41
十九年十一月奏，倭酋關白平秀吉聲言明年三月來犯，詔兵部申飭海防。 平秀吉者，薩摩州人，初隨倭關白信長。 會信長為其下所弑，秀吉遂統信長兵，自號關白，劫降六十餘州。 朝鮮與日本對馬島相望，時有倭夷往來互市。 二十年夏五月，秀吉遂分渠帥行長、清正等率舟師逼釜山鎮，潛渡臨津。 時朝鮮承平久，兵不習戰，昖又湎酒，弛備，猝島夷作難，望風皆潰。 昖棄王城，令次子琿攝國事，奔平壤。 已，復走義州，願內屬。 七月，兵部議令駐劄險要，以待天兵； 號召通國勤王，以圖恢復。 而是時倭已入王京，毀墳墓，劫王子、陪臣，剽府庫，八道幾盡沒，旦暮且渡鴨綠江，請援之使絡繹於道。 廷議以朝鮮為國籓籬，在所必爭。 遣行人薛潘諭昖以興復大義，揚言大兵十萬且至。 而倭業抵平壤，朝鮮君臣益急，出避愛州。 遊擊史儒等率師至平壤，戰死。 副總兵祖承訓統兵渡鴨綠江援之，僅以身免。 中朝震動，以宋應昌為經略。 八月，倭入豐德等郡，兵部尚書石星計無所出，議遣人偵探之，於是嘉興人沈惟敬應募。 惟敬者，市中無賴也。 是時秀吉次對馬島，分其將行長等守要害為聲援。 惟敬至平壤，執禮其卑。 行長紿曰：「天朝幸按兵不動，我不久當還。 以大同江為界，平壤以西盡屬朝鮮耳。 」惟敬以聞。 廷議倭詐未可信，乃趣應昌等進兵。 而星頗惑於惟敬，乃題署遊擊，赴軍前，且請金行間。 十二月，以李如松為東征提督。 明年正月，如松督諸將進戰，大捷於平壤。 行長渡大同江，遁還龍山。 所失黃海、平安、京畿、江原四道並復，清正亦遁還王京。 如松既勝，輕騎趨碧蹄館，敗，退駐開城。 事具《如松傳》。
In the eleventh month of the nineteenth year a memorial reported that the Wa chieftain the regent Hideyoshi declared he would invade in the third month of the following year; an edict ordered the Ministry of War to tighten coastal defenses. Hideyoshi was a man of Satsuma province who initially served the Wa regent Nobunaga. When Nobunaga was assassinated by his subordinates, Hideyoshi took command of Nobunaga's armies, styled himself regent, and by force and surrender subjugated more than sixty provinces. Korea and Japan's Tsushima Island face each other across the sea, and Wa traders came and went between them. In the fifth month of summer in the twentieth year Hideyoshi sent his commanders Yukinaga, Kiyomasa, and others at the head of a fleet against Busan garrison and secretly crossed the Imjin. Korea had long enjoyed peace, its troops were unaccustomed to war, and Seon drowned himself in wine and neglected defenses; when the island barbarians suddenly rose in revolt, the armies fled at the mere sight of the enemy. Seon abandoned the royal capital, ordered his second son Hui to administer state affairs, and fled to Pyongyang. Soon afterward he fled again to Uiju and requested to submit to Ming protection. In the seventh month the Ministry of War deliberated ordering him to hold fast at strategic points and await the Celestial army; to summon the whole country to defend the throne and plan the recovery of the realm. But by then the Wa had already entered the royal capital, destroyed tombs, seized princes and attendant ministers, and plundered treasuries; nearly all eight provinces were lost and they were on the verge of crossing the Yalu River at any moment; envoys begging for aid thronged the roads. Court deliberation held that Korea was the outer bulwark of the realm and must be defended at all costs. The emissary Xue Pan was dispatched to instruct Seon in the great principle of restoration and to proclaim that a hundred thousand Ming troops would soon arrive. But the Wa had already reached Pyongyang; the Korean king and ministers grew still more desperate and withdrew to Aiju. Guerrilla commander Shi Ru and others led troops to Pyongyang and died in battle. Vice commander-in-chief Zu Chengxun led troops across the Yalu River to aid them and barely escaped with his life. The Central Court was shaken, and Song Yingchang was appointed strategic coordinator. In the eighth month the Wa entered Pungdok and other prefectures; Minister of War Shi Xing could devise no plan and proposed sending someone to reconnoiter, and Shen Weijing of Jiaxing answered the call. Weijing was a marketplace ruffian. At that time Hideyoshi was stationed at Tsushima Island and posted his generals Yukinaga and others at strategic points as a supporting force. Weijing reached Pyongyang and abased himself in the most servile manner. Yukinaga deceived him, saying: "The Celestial Court has fortunately held its troops in check; I shall soon withdraw. With the Taedong River as the boundary, everything west of Pyongyang will belong to Korea alone. " Weijing reported this to the court. Court deliberation held that the Wa could not be trusted and urged Song Yingchang and others to advance. But Shi Xing was quite taken in by Weijing; he granted him the title of guerrilla commander and sent him to the front, and moreover requested gold for covert operations. In the twelfth month Li Rusong was appointed overall commander of the eastern expedition. In the first month of the following year Rusong led the generals into battle and won a great victory at Pyongyang. Yukinaga crossed the Taedong River and fled back to Ryongsan. The four lost provinces of Hwanghae, Pyongan, Gyeonggi, and Gangwon were all recovered, and Kiyomasa also fled back to the royal capital. After his victory Rusong pressed forward with light cavalry toward Pyeokjicheon garrison, was defeated, and withdrew to Kaesong. The full account is given in the Biography of Li Rusong.
42
初，如松誓師，欲斬惟敬，以參軍李應試言而止。 至是敗，氣縮，而應昌急圖成功，倭亦乏食有歸志，因而封貢之議起。 應昌得倭報惟敬書，乃令遊擊周弘謨同惟敬往諭倭，獻王京，返王子，如約縱歸。 倭果于四月棄王城遁。 時漢江以南千有餘里朝鮮故土復定，兵部言宜令王還國居守，我各鎮兵久疲海外，以次撤歸為便。 詔可。 應昌疏稱：「釜山雖瀕海南，猶朝鮮境，有如倭覘我罷兵，突入再犯，朝鮮不支，前功盡棄。 今撥兵協守為第一策，即議撤，宜少需，俟倭盡歸，量留防戍。 」部議留江浙兵五千，分屯要害，仍諭昖搜練軍實，毋恃外援。 已而沈惟敬歸自釜山，同倭使來請款，而倭隨犯咸安、晉州，逼全羅，聲復漢江以南，以王京、漢江為界。 如松計全羅饒沃，南原府尤其咽喉，乃命諸將分守要害。 已，倭果分犯，我師並有斬獲。 兵科給事中張輔之、遼東都御史趙耀皆言款貢不可輕受。 七月，倭從釜山移西生浦，送回王子、陪臣。 時師久暴露，聞撤，勢難久羈。 應昌請留劉綎川兵，吳惟忠、駱尚志等南兵，合薊、遼兵共萬六千，聽綎分佈尚之大丘，月餉五萬兩，資之戶兵二部。 先是，發帑給軍費，已累百萬。 廷臣言虛內實外非長策，請以所留川兵命綎訓練，兵餉令本國自辦。 於是詔撤惟忠等兵，止留綎兵防守。 諭朝鮮世子臨海君珒居全慶，以顧養謙為經略。 九月，昖以三都既復，疆域再造，上表謝恩。 然時倭猶據釜山也，星益一意主款。 九月，兵部主事曾偉芳言：「關白大眾已還，行長留待。 知我兵未撤，不敢以一矢加遺。 欲歸報關白捲土重來，則風不利，正苦冬寒。 故款亦去，不款亦去。 沈惟敬前于倭營講購，咸安、晉州隨陷，而俗恃款冀來年不攻，則速之款者，正速之來耳。 故款亦來，不款亦來。 宜令朝鮮自為守，吊死問孤，練兵積粟，以圖自強。 」帝以為然，因敕諭昖者甚至。
At the outset, when Rusong mustered the army, he wished to execute Weijing but desisted on the advice of staff officer Li Yingshi. After this defeat morale collapsed; Song Yingchang urgently sought a settlement; the Wa also lacked provisions and wished to withdraw; and thus arose deliberation over investiture and tribute. Song Yingchang received a Wa report and Weijing's letter and ordered guerrilla commander Zhou Hongmo together with Weijing to instruct the Wa to surrender the royal capital, return the princes, and release captives as agreed. The Wa indeed abandoned the royal city and fled in the fourth month. At that time more than a thousand li of Korean territory south of the Han River had been restored; the Ministry of War argued that the king should be ordered to return and hold the country while our garrison troops, long exhausted overseas, should be withdrawn in turn. An edict approved this. Song Yingchang memorialized: "Although Busan borders the sea to the south, it is still Korean territory; if the Wa observe our withdrawal of troops and suddenly invade again, Korea cannot hold out and all previous gains will be lost. Assigning troops for joint defense is the best course; even if withdrawal is contemplated, a short delay is appropriate—wait until the Wa have all returned, then leave a measured garrison force. " The ministry deliberated leaving five thousand Jiangsu and Zhejiang troops garrisoned at strategic points and instructed Seon to search out and drill his military strength and not rely on external aid. Soon afterward Shen Weijing returned from Busan together with a Wa envoy to sue for peace, but the Wa then invaded Haman and Jinju, pressed into Jeolla, and declared they would recover the territory south of the Han River, with the royal capital and the Han River as the boundary. Rusong judged Jeolla rich and fertile and Namwon prefecture especially its vital pass; he ordered the generals to divide forces and hold the strategic points. Soon afterward the Wa indeed divided forces to invade, and our armies both killed and captured the enemy. Supervising secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Fuzhi and Liaodong censor-in-chief Zhao Yao both argued that peace overtures and tribute should not be lightly accepted. In the seventh month the Wa moved from Busan to Saseongpo and returned the princes and attendant ministers. The army had long been exposed to the elements; on hearing of withdrawal, it was difficult to keep them under restraint much longer. Song Yingchang requested leaving Liu Ting's Sichuan troops together with Wu Weizhong, Luo Shangzhi, and other southern troops, combined with Ji and Liaodong troops totaling sixteen thousand; Ting was to distribute them with Shangzhi at Daegu, with monthly rations of fifty thousand taels supplied by the Ministries of Revenue and War. Previously, disbursements from the treasury for military expenses had already totaled more than a million taels. Court officials argued that emptying the interior to strengthen the exterior was no long-term strategy; they requested that the Sichuan troops left behind be placed under Ting for training and that military rations be supplied by Korea itself. Thereupon an edict ordered the withdrawal of Wu Weizhong's troops and others, leaving only Ting's troops for defense. The Korean heir apparent Imhaegun Jeong was instructed to reside at Jeonju, and Gu Yangqian was appointed strategic coordinator. In the ninth month Seon, because the three capitals had been recovered and the realm restored, submitted a memorial of thanks. Yet at that time the Wa still held Busan, and Shi Xing increasingly insisted on peace alone. In the ninth month Bureau of Military Affairs section chief Zeng Weifang stated: "The regent's main force has already returned; Yukinaga remains waiting. Knowing our troops have not withdrawn, he dares not add a single arrow to the remnant force. If he wishes to return and report to the regent to gather his forces and come again, the winds are unfavorable and he suffers from the winter cold. Therefore whether there is peace or not, he will leave. Previously Shen Weijing negotiated purchase in the Wa camp, and Haman and Jinju then fell; yet the people relied on peace hoping for no attack next year—those who hasten peace are precisely those who hasten the coming attack. Therefore whether there is peace or not, he will come. Korea should be ordered to defend itself, comfort the dead and inquire after the orphaned, drill troops and store grain, and plan to strengthen itself. " The emperor thought this correct and issued edicts instructing Seon to an extraordinary degree.
43
二十二年正月，昖遣金晬等進方物謝恩。 禮部郎中何喬遠奏：「晬涕泣言倭寇猖獗，朝鮮束手受刃者六萬餘人。 倭語悖慢無禮，沈惟敬與倭交通，不雲和親，輒曰乞降。 臣謹將萬曆十九年中國被掠人許儀所寄內地書、倭夷答劉綎書及歷年入寇處置之宜，乞特敕急止封貢。 」詔兵部議。 時廷臣交章，皆以罷封貢、議戰守為言。 八月，養謙奏講貢之說，貢道宜從寧波，關白宜封為日本王，諭行長部倭盡歸，與封貢如約。 九月，昖請許保國。 帝乃切責群臣阻撓，追褫御史郭實等。 詔小西飛入朝，集多官面議，要以三事：一，勒倭盡歸巢； 一，既封不與貢； 一，誓無犯朝鮮。 倭俱聽從，以聞。 帝復諭于左闕，語加周復。 十二月，封議定，命臨淮侯李宗城充正使，以都指揮楊方亨副之，同沈惟敬往日本，王給金印，行長授都督僉事。
In the first month of the twenty-second year Seon dispatched Kim Chun and others to present local products in thanks. Bureau director of the Ministry of Rites He Qiaoyuan memorialized: "Chun wept and stated that the Wa pirates were rampant; more than sixty thousand people in Korea had helplessly submitted to the blade. Wa speech was insolent and without propriety; Shen Weijing communicated with the Wa; instead of speaking of marriage alliance, he spoke of begging surrender. Your subject respectfully submits the letter from the interior sent by Xu Yi, a Chinese captive in the nineteenth year of Wanli, the Wa barbarians' reply to Liu Ting, and the proper disposition of raids over the years, and begs for a special edict urgently stopping investiture and tribute. " An edict ordered the Ministry of War to deliberate. At that time court officials submitted memorial after memorial, all arguing to stop investiture and tribute and to deliberate war and defense. In the eighth month Yangqian memorialized on the plan for tribute negotiations: the tribute route should be from Ningbo; the regent should be enfeoffed as King of Japan; Yukinaga's Wa forces should be instructed to all return, and investiture and tribute should proceed as agreed. In the ninth month Seon requested permission to preserve the state. The emperor thereupon sharply rebuked the officials for obstruction and stripped Censor Guo Shi and others of their posts. An edict summoned Konishi Hi to court; many officials were assembled for face-to-face deliberation, requiring three matters: first, compel the Wa to all return home; second, once enfeoffed, no tribute is granted; third, swear not to violate Korea. The Wa all agreed; this was reported to the throne. The emperor again instructed at the Left Gate, his words thorough and repeated. In the twelfth month the investiture plan was settled; Marquis of Linhuai Li Zongcheng was appointed chief envoy, with Regional Commander Yang Fangheng as deputy, together with Shen Weijing to go to Japan; the king was given a gold seal and Yukinaga was granted the post of assistant regional commander.
44
二十三年九月，昖奏立次子琿為嗣。 先是，昖庶長子臨海君珒陷賊中，驚憂成疾，次子光海君琿收集流散，頗著功績，奏請立之。 禮部尚書范謙言繼統大義，長幼定分，不宜僭差，遂不許。 至是復奏，引永樂間恭定王例上請，禮臣執奏，不從。 二十四年五月，昖復疏請立琿，禮部仍執不可，詔如議。 時國儲未建，中外恫疑，故尚書范謙于朝鮮易封事三疏力持雲。
In the ninth month of the twenty-third year Seon memorialized to establish his second son Hui as heir. Previously Seon's eldest son by a concubine, Imhaegun Jeong, had been trapped among the enemy and fell ill from alarm and grief; the second son Gwanghaegun Hui gathered the scattered population and achieved considerable merit, and a memorial requested that he be established as heir. Minister of Rites Fan Qian cited the great principle of succession—that elder and younger have a fixed order and should not be improperly altered—and permission was denied. At this time a memorial was again submitted, citing the precedent of King Gongding in the Yongle period; the rites officials firmly memorialized in opposition and it was not approved. In the fifth month of the twenty-fourth year Seon again memorialized requesting that Hui be established as heir; the Ministry of Rites still firmly opposed it, and an edict followed their deliberation. At that time no heir to the state had been established and there was alarm and doubt at court and abroad; therefore, on the matter of Korea's requested change of succession, Minister Fan Qian submitted three memorials firmly maintaining his dissent.
45
九月，封使至日本。 先是，沈惟敬抵釜山，私奉秀吉蟒玉、翼善冠、地圖、武經、良馬。 而李宗城以貪淫為倭守臣所逐，棄璽書夜遁。 事聞，逮問。 乃以方亨充正使，加惟敬神機營銜副之。 及是奉冊至，關白怒朝鮮王子不來謝，止遣二使奉白土綢為賀，拒其使不見，語惟敬曰：「若不思二子、三大臣、三都、八道悉遵天朝約付還，今以卑官微物來賀，辱小邦邪？ 辱天朝邪？ 且留石曼子兵於彼，候天朝處分，然後撤還。 」翌日奉貢，遣使齎表文二道，隨冊使渡海至朝鮮。 廷議遣使於朝鮮，取表文進驗，其一謝恩，其一乞天子處分朝鮮。
In the ninth month the investiture envoys arrived in Japan. Previously, Shen Weijing reached Busan and on his own authority presented Hideyoshi with python-pattern jade ornaments, the Yishan cap, maps, military treatises, and fine horses. Meanwhile Li Zongcheng, for greed and licentiousness, was driven off by the Wa garrison officials; he abandoned the imperial seal and credentials and fled under cover of night. When the matter was reported, he was arrested and brought to trial. Thereupon Yang Fangheng was appointed chief envoy, with Shen Weijing added as deputy bearing the rank of the Divine Engine Corps. When the investiture credentials arrived, the regent was enraged that the Korean prince had not come to give thanks and sent only two envoys bearing white silk earth cloth as congratulation. He refused to receive the envoys and told Weijing, "If you do not intend that the two princes, the three ministers, the three capitals, and the eight provinces all be returned as the Celestial Court agreed, and now send a low-ranking official with trivial gifts to congratulate us, is this meant to insult our small state? Or to insult the Celestial Court?" Moreover, leave Ishimanzhi's troops there until the Celestial Court decides, and only then withdraw them. The next day he presented tribute and dispatched envoys bearing two memorials, crossing the sea with the investiture envoys to Korea. The court deliberated on dispatching envoys to Korea to retrieve the memorials and submit them for verification—one expressing thanks, the other requesting the Son of Heaven's disposition of Korea.
46
初，方亨詭報去年從釜山渡海，倭於大版受封，即回和泉州。 然倭方責備朝鮮，仍留兵釜山如故，謝表後時不發，方亨徒手歸。 至是，惟敬始投表文，案驗潦草，前折用豐臣圖書，不奉正朔，無人臣禮。 而寬奠副總兵馬楝報清正擁二百艘屯機張營。 方亨始直吐本末，委罪惟敬，並呈石星前後手書。 帝大怒，命逮石星、沈惟敬案問。 以兵部尚書邢玠總督薊、遼； 改麻貴為備倭大將軍，經理朝鮮； 僉都御史楊鎬駐天津，申警備； 楊汝南、丁應泰贊畫軍前。
Initially Fangheng had falsely reported that the previous year, after crossing the sea from Busan, the Wa received investiture at Osaka and immediately returned to Izumi. Yet the Wa were still pressing Korea and keeping troops at Busan as before; the thank-you memorial was slow in coming, and Fangheng returned empty-handed. At this point Weijing at last submitted the memorials; examination found them careless—they had used Toyotomi's own documents, did not observe the correct calendar, and lacked the courtesies due a subject. Meanwhile Kuandian deputy regional commander Ma Dong reported that Kiyomasa had two hundred ships encamped at Gijang. Fangheng at last told the whole story plainly, shifted the blame onto Weijing, and also submitted Shi Xing's letters from before and after. The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered Shi Xing and Shen Weijing arrested and brought to trial. Minister of War Xing Jie was appointed grand coordinator of Ji and Liaodong; Ma Gui was reassigned as Great General for Preparedness against Wa to administer Korea; Censor-in-Chief Yang Hao was stationed at Tianjin to raise the alarm and strengthen defenses; Yang Runnan and Ding Yingtai served as staff planners at the front.
47
五月，玠至遼。 行長建樓，清正布種，島倭窖水，索朝鮮地圖，玠遂決意用兵。 麻貴望鴨綠江東發，所統兵僅萬七千人，請濟師。 玠以朝鮮兵惟嫻水戰，乃疏請募兵川、浙，並調薊、遼、宣、大、山、陝兵及福建、吳淞水師，劉綎督川、漢兵聽剿。 貴密報候宣、大兵至，乘倭未備，掩釜山，則行長擒，清正走。 玠以為奇計，乃檄楊元屯南原，吳惟忠屯忠州。
In the fifth month Xing Jie reached Liaodong. Yukinaga built towers, Kiyomasa planted crops, the island Wa stockpiled water, and they demanded Korean maps; Xing Jie thereupon resolved to take military action. Ma Gui looked to advance from the east bank of the Yalu River, but the troops under his command numbered only seventeen thousand; he requested reinforcements. Xing Jie, judging that Korean troops were skilled only in naval combat, memorialized requesting recruitment from Sichuan and Zhejiang and also mobilized troops from Ji, Liaodong, Xuanfu, Datong, Shanxi, and Shaanxi, along with the Fujian and Wusong naval forces, assigning Liu Ting to direct Sichuan and Han troops for extermination duty. Gui secretly reported that when the Xuanfu and Datong troops arrived, they should strike Busan while the Wa were unprepared—then Yukinaga would be captured and Kiyomasa would flee. Xing Jie regarded this as a brilliant stratagem and ordered Yang Yuan to encamp at Namwon and Wu Weizhong at Chungju.
48
六月，倭數千艘泊釜山，戮朝鮮郡守安弘國，漸逼梁山、熊川。 惟敬率營兵二百，出入釜山。 玠陽為慰藉，檄楊元襲執之，縛至貴營，惟敬執而嚮導始絕。 七月，倭奪梁山、三浪，遂入慶州，侵閑山。 統制元均兵潰，遂失閑山。 閑山島在朝鮮西海口，右障南原，為全羅外籓，一失守則沿海無備，天津、登、萊皆可揚帆而至。 而我水兵三千甫抵旅順，閑山破，經略檄守王京西之漢江、大同江，扼倭西下，兼防運道。
In the sixth month several thousand Wa ships anchored at Busan, executed the Korean prefect An Hongguo, and gradually pressed toward Yangsan and Ungcheon. Weijing led two hundred camp soldiers in and out of Busan. Xing Jie feigned consolation while ordering Yang Yuan to seize him in a surprise raid; Weijing was bound and sent to Gui's camp, and with his capture the guiding liaison was finally severed. In the seventh month the Wa took Yangsan and Sannang, then entered Gyeongju and invaded Hansan. Commander Won Gyun's army collapsed, and Hansan was lost. Hansan Island lay at Korea's western sea mouth, shielding Namwon on the right as Jeolla's outer defense; once it fell the coast was undefended, and Tianjin, Dengzhou, and Laizhou could all be reached under sail. Our three thousand naval troops had just reached Lüshun when Hansan fell; the grand coordinator ordered troops to hold the Han River and Taedong River west of the royal capital, blocking the Wa from descending westward while also guarding the supply routes.
49
八月，清正圍南原，乘夜猝攻，守將楊元遁。 時全州有陳愚衷，去南原僅百里，南原告急，愚衷不敢救，聞已破，棄城走。 麻貴遣遊擊牛伯英赴援，與愚衷合兵，屯公州。 倭遂犯全慶，逼王京。 王京為朝鮮八道之中，東阻烏嶺、忠州，西則南原、全州，道相通。 自二城失，東西皆倭，我兵單弱，因退守王京，依險漢江。 麻貴請於玠欲棄王京退守鴨綠江。 海防使蕭應宮以為不可，自平壤兼程趨王京止之。 麻貴發兵守稷山，朝鮮亦調都體察使李元翼由烏嶺出忠清道遮賊鋒。 玠既身赴王京，人心始定。 玠召參軍李應試問計，應試請問廟廷主畫雲何。 玠曰：「陽戰陰和，陽剿陰撫，政府八字密畫，無泄也。 應試曰：「然則易耳。 倭叛以處分絕望，其不敢殺楊元，猶望處分也。 直使人諭之曰沈惟敬不死，則退矣。 」因請使李大諫于行長，馮仲纓於清正，玠從之。 九月，倭至漢江，楊鎬遣張貞明持惟敬手書往，責其動兵，有乖靜候處分之實。 行長、正成亦尤清正輕舉，乃退屯井邑。 麻貴遂報青山、稷山大捷。 蕭應宮揭言：「倭以惟敬手書而退，青山、稷山並未接戰，何得言功？ 」玠、鎬怒，遂劾應宮恇怯，不親解惟敬，並逮。
In the eighth month Kiyomasa besieged Namwon and struck suddenly by night; the defending general Yang Yuan fled. At that time Chen Enzhong was at Jeonju, only a hundred li from Namwon; Namwon urgently called for aid, but Enzhong dared not go to its rescue, and when he heard it had fallen he abandoned the city and fled. Ma Gui dispatched raiding colonel Niu Boying to aid them; Boying joined Enzhong's forces and encamped at Gongju. The Wa then invaded Jeolla and Gyeongsang and pressed toward the royal capital. The royal capital stood at the center of Korea's eight provinces; to the east it was blocked by Wolyeong and Chungju, to the west lay Namwon and Jeonju, with roads linking them. With both cities lost, Wa forces lay to east and west; our troops were few and weak, so we withdrew to hold the royal capital, taking the Han River's natural defenses. Ma Gui asked Xing Jie about abandoning the royal capital and withdrawing to defend the Yalu River. Coastal defense commissioner Xiao Yinggong held this impossible and raced from Pyongyang by forced marches to the royal capital to stop it. Ma Gui sent troops to hold Mt. Jiri; Korea also mobilized provincial inspector Li Yuanyi to go out through Wolyeong into Chungcheong route to block the enemy vanguard. Once Xing Jie himself went to the royal capital, morale began to settle. Xing Jie summoned staff officer Li Yingxi to ask his plan; Yingxi asked what the court's chief strategy was. Xing Jie said, "Openly fight but secretly treat for peace; openly exterminate but secretly pacify—the government has eight confidential characters for its plan; do not leak them. Yingxi said, "Then it is easy. The Wa rebel because they despair of receiving disposition; that they dare not kill Yang Yuan shows they still hope for disposition. Simply send someone to tell them: if Shen Weijing is not dead, they will withdraw. Thereupon he requested that Li Dajian be sent to Yukinaga and Feng Zhongying to Kiyomasa; Xing Jie agreed. In the ninth month the Wa reached the Han River; Yang Hao sent Zhang Zhenming with Weijing's handwritten letter, reproaching them for moving troops in violation of quietly awaiting disposition. Yukinaga and Seisei also blamed Kiyomasa for reckless action and withdrew to encamp at Jeup. Ma Gui thereupon reported great victories at Cheongsan and Mt. Jiri. Xiao Yinggong publicly stated, "The Wa withdrew because of Weijing's handwritten letter; at Cheongsan and Mt. Jiri there was no engagement at all—how can victory be claimed? Xing Jie and Hao were enraged and memorialized against Yinggong for cowardice and for not personally securing Weijing's release; he was arrested as well.
50
十一月，玠徵兵大集，帝發帑金犒軍，賜玠尚方劍，而以御史陳效監其軍。 玠大會諸將，分三協。 鎬同貴率左右協，自忠州、烏嶺向東安，趨慶州，專攻清正。 使李大諫通行長，約勿往援。 復遣中協屯宜城，東援慶州，西扼全羅。 以餘兵會朝鮮合營，詐攻順天等處，以牽制行長東援。 十二月，會慶州。 麻貴遣黃慶賜賄清正約和，而率大兵奄至其營。 時倭屯蔚山，城依山險，中一江通釜寨，其陸路由彥陽通釜山。 貴欲專攻蔚山，恐釜倭由彥陽來援，乃多張疑兵，又遣將遏其水路，遂進逼倭壘。 遊擊擺寨以輕騎誘倭入伏，斬級四百餘，獲其勇將，乘勝拔兩柵。 倭焚死者無算，遂奔島山，連築三寨。 翌日，遊擊茅國器統浙兵先登，連破之，斬獲甚多，倭堅壁不出。 島山視蔚山高，石城堅甚，我師仰攻多損傷。 諸將乃議曰：「倭艱水道，餉難繼，第坐困之，清正可不戰縛也。 」鎬等以為然，分兵圍十日夜，倭饑甚，偽約降緩攻。 俄行長援兵大至，將繞出軍後。 鎬不及下令，策馬西奔，諸軍皆潰。 遂撤兵還王京，士卒物故者二萬。 上聞之，震怒。 乃罷鎬聽勘，以天津巡撫萬世德代。 事詳《鎬傳》。
In the eleventh month Xing Jie gathered a great muster of troops; the emperor issued treasury gold to reward the army, granted Xing Jie the imperial sword, and appointed censor Chen Xiao to supervise the army. Xing Jie held a great assembly of generals and divided them into three wings. Hao together with Gui led the left and right wings from Chungju and Wolyeong toward Dongan, pressing to Gyeongju to concentrate the attack on Kiyomasa. Li Dajian was sent to Yukinaga with an agreement not to go to his aid. The center wing was again dispatched to encamp at Uiseong, aiding Gyeongju to the east and blocking Jeolla to the west. The remaining troops joined the Korean combined camp and feigned attacks on Suncheon and other places to tie down Yukinaga's eastern relief. In the twelfth month they assembled at Gyeongju. Ma Gui sent Huang Qing with bribes to Kiyomasa to arrange peace while leading a large force to suddenly arrive at his camp. At that time the Wa were encamped at Ulsan; the city leaned on mountain defenses, with a river in the middle connecting to the Busan stockade, and the land route passed through Uiryeong to Busan. Gui wished to concentrate on attacking Ulsan; fearing Busan Wa would come to aid via Uiryeong, he deployed many feints, sent generals to block their water route, and then advanced to press the Wa fortifications. The raiding colonel deployed camps and used light cavalry to lure the Wa into an ambush, beheading more than four hundred, capturing their brave general, and seizing two palisades in the momentum of victory. Countless Wa died in the fires; they then fled to Dolsan and built three camps in succession. The next day raiding colonel Mao Guoqi leading Zhejiang troops mounted the assault first, broke through in succession with many beheaded and captured, and the Wa held their walls and did not come out. Dolsan overlooked Ulsan and stood higher; the stone walls were very strong, and our army attacking upward suffered many casualties. The generals then deliberated, "The Wa lack water routes and supplies are hard to sustain—simply sit and wear them down, and Kiyomasa can be bound without battle. Hao and others agreed; troops were divided to besiege for ten day-nights; the Wa were very hungry and falsely promised surrender to slow the attack. Suddenly Yukinaga's relief force arrived in great strength and was about to swing around behind the army. Hao had no time to issue orders; he spurred his horse and fled west, and all the armies collapsed. They thereupon withdrew to the royal capital; twenty thousand soldiers had perished. When the emperor heard, he was shaken with rage. Hao was dismissed pending investigation, and Tianjin grand coordinator Wan Shide was appointed in his place. Details are in the biography of Hao.
51
二十六年正月，邢玠以前役乏水兵無功，乃益募江南水兵，議海運，為持久計。 二月，都督陳璘以廣兵，劉綎以川兵，鄧子龍以浙、直兵先後至。 玠分兵三協，為水陸四路，路置大將。 中路如梅，東路貴，西路綎，水路璘，各守汛地，相機行剿。 時倭亦分三窟。 東路則清正，據蔚山。 西路則行長，據粟林、曳橋，建砦數重。 中路則石曼子，據泗州。 而行長水師番休濟餉，往來如駛。 我師約日並進，尋報遼陽警，李如松敗沒，詔如梅還赴之，中路以董一元代。
In the first month of the twenty-sixth year Xing Jie, because the previous campaign had lacked naval troops and achieved nothing, further recruited Jiangnan naval soldiers, deliberated on sea transport, and planned for a protracted struggle. In the second month Regional Commander Chen Lin arrived with Guangdong troops, Liu Ting with Sichuan troops, and Deng Zilong with Zhejiang and Zhili troops, arriving in succession. Xing Jie divided troops into three wings, forming four routes by land and water, each route with a senior commander. The center route was Li Rumei, the east route Gui, the west route Ting, and the water route Lin; each held their assigned sector and acted on opportunity to exterminate the enemy. At that time the Wa also divided into three lairs. The east route was Kiyomasa, holding Ulsan. The west route was Yukinaga, holding Awlin and Yegeo and building several layers of forts. The center route was Ishimanzhi, holding Sacheon. Meanwhile Yukinaga's navy rotated shifts to supply provisions, coming and going like flying arrows. Our army agreed to advance on the same day; soon came word of an alarm at Liaoyang and that Li Rusong had been defeated and killed; an edict ordered Rumei to return to meet it, and Dong Yiyuan replaced him on the center route.
52
當應泰之劾鎬也，昖請回乾斷，崇勵鎮撫，以畢征討。 上不許。 又應泰曾以築城之議為鎬罪案，謂堅城得志，啟朝鮮異日之患，於是昖奏辨。 帝曰：「連年用兵發餉，以爾國素效忠順故也，毋以人言自疑。」
When Yingtai memorialized against Hao, Seon requested restored imperial decision and exalted encouragement and pacification to complete the punitive expedition. The emperor did not permit it. Moreover Yingtai had made fortification proposals part of Hao's criminal case, stating that strong walls gratified ambition and would open Korea to future troubles; Seon thereupon memorialized in defense. The emperor said, "Year after year we have deployed troops and issued supplies because your state has long shown loyal obedience; do not let others' words make you doubt yourselves."
53
九月，將士分道進兵，劉綎進逼行長營，約行長為好會。 翌日，攻城，斬首九十二。 陳璘舟師協堵擊，毀倭船百餘。 行長潛出千餘騎扼之，綎不利，退，璘亦棄舟走。 麻貴至蔚山，頗有斬獲，倭偽退誘之。 貴入空壘，伏兵起，遂敗。 董一元進取晉州，乘勝渡江，連毀二寨。 倭退保泗州老營，鏖戰下之，前逼新寨。 寨三面臨江，一面通陸，引海為濠，海艘泊寨下千計，築金海、固城為左右翼。 十月，董一元遣將四面攻城，用火器擊碎寨門，兵競前拔柵。 忽營中火藥崩，煙焰漲天。 倭乘勢衝擊，固城倭亦至，兵遂大潰，奔還晉州。 帝聞，命斬二遊擊以徇，一元等各帶罪立功。 是月，福建都御史金學曾報七月九日平秀吉死，各倭俱有歸志。 十一月，清正發舟先走，麻貴遂入島山、酉浦，劉綎攻奪曳橋。 石曼子引舟師救行長，陳璘邀擊敗之。 諸倭揚帆盡歸。 自倭亂朝鮮七載，喪師數十萬，糜餉數百萬，中朝與屬國迄無勝算，至關白死而禍始息。
In the ninth month officers and soldiers advanced by separate routes; Liu Ting pressed close to Yukinaga's camp and arranged a friendly meeting with him. The next day they assaulted the city and beheaded ninety-two. Chen Lin's fleet joined in blocking and striking, destroying more than a hundred Wa ships. Yukinaga secretly sent out more than a thousand cavalry to block them; Ting fared poorly and withdrew, and Lin also abandoned his ships and fled.
