Ma Gui reached Ulsan and had considerable beheadings and captures; the Wa feigned retreat to lure him. Gui entered the empty fort; ambush troops rose, and he was defeated. Dong Yiyuan advanced to take Jinju, crossed the river on the momentum of victory, and destroyed two camps in succession. The Wa retreated to hold Sacheon's old camp; after fierce fighting it was taken, and they pressed forward to the new camp. The camp faced the river on three sides and connected to land on one; seawater was drawn in as a moat; a thousand sea vessels moored beneath the camp; Jinhae and Goseong were fortified as left and right wings. In the tenth month Dong Yiyuan dispatched generals to assault the city from four sides; fire weapons shattered the camp gates and troops rushed forward to seize the palisades. Without warning, gunpowder in the camp detonated, and smoke and fire billowed skyward. The Japanese forces pressed the attack; reinforcements from Goseong joined them, and the Ming army broke completely and fled back to Jinju. On hearing this, the Emperor ordered two detached commanders executed as an example; Dong Yiyuan and the rest were ordered to win back their honor through service. That month Jin Xuezeng, provincial surveillance commissioner of Fujian, reported that Hideyoshi had died on the ninth day of the seventh month and that the Japanese troops were ready to withdraw. In the eleventh month Kato Kiyomasa sailed away ahead of the others; Ma Gui advanced into Island Mountain and Yupo, while Liu Ting stormed and took Yegyo Bridge. Ishida Mitsunari brought a naval force to relieve Konishi Yukinaga, but Chen Lin intercepted and routed him. The Japanese forces hoisted sail and sailed home. The war in Korea had lasted seven years, costing hundreds of thousands of lives and millions in supplies, and neither the Ming nor its ally had found a path to victory—until Hideyoshi’s death finally brought the disaster to an end.
54
二十七年閏四月，以平倭詔告天下，又敕諭昖曰：「倭奴平秀吉肆為不道，蹂躪爾邦。 朕念王世篤忠貞，深用憫惻。 七年之中，日以此賊為事。 始行薄伐，繼示包容，終加嚴討。 蓋不殺乃天之心，而用兵非予得已。 安疆靖亂，宜取蕩平。 神惡凶盈，陰殲魁首，大師乘之，追奔逐北，鯨鯢盡戮，海隅載清，捷書來聞，憂勞始釋。 惟王雖還舊物，實同新造，振凋起敝，為力倍艱。 倭雖遁歸，族類尚在。 茲命邢玠振旅歸京，量留萬世德等分佈戍守。 王宜臥薪嚐膽，無忘前恥，惟忠惟孝，纘紹前休。 」五月，玠條陳東征善後事宜十事。 一，留戍兵，馬步水陸共計三萬四千有奇，馬三千匹。 一，定月餉，每年計銀九十一萬八千有奇。 一，定本色，合用米豆，分派遼東、天津、山東等處，每年十三萬石。 一，留中路海防道。 一，裁餉司。 一，重將領。 一，添巡捕。 一，分汛地。 一，議操練。 一，責成本國。 廷臣議：「數年疲耗，今始息肩，自宜內固根本，不當更為繁費。 況彼國兵荒之後，不獨苦倭之擾，兼苦我兵。 故今日善後事宜，仍當商之彼國，先量彼餉之贏絀，始可酌我兵之去留。 至於增買馬匹，添補標兵，創立巡捕，及至管餉府佐，悉宜停止。 」帝命督撫會同國王酌奏。 八月，昖獻方物，助大工，褒賞如例。 十月，請留水兵八千，以資戍守。 其撤回官兵，駐劄遼陽備警。 二十八年四月請將義州等倉遺下米豆運回遼陽。 戶部議：「輸運維艱，莫若徑與彼國，振其雕敝，以昭皇仁。 」詔曰：「可。」
In the intercalary fourth month of year twenty-seven the court proclaimed to the empire that the Japanese invasion had been pacified, and the Emperor also addressed Seonjo: "The Japanese brigand Hideyoshi committed outrageous crimes and ravaged your kingdom." I have long regarded Your Majesty as steadfast in loyalty and integrity, and my heart is full of compassion for your suffering. For seven years this enemy was the business that occupied us day after day. We began with a limited punitive expedition, then offered forbearance, and at last brought down stern retribution. Heaven’s way is to spare life, yet I had no choice but to take up arms. To secure the frontier and restore peace, nothing less than total pacification would suffice. Heaven abhors those whose wickedness overflows; the chief culprit was struck down in secret. Our great army seized the moment, pursued the fleeing enemy, and destroyed them root and branch until the coast was clear. When the victory dispatches arrived, my cares at last began to lift. Though you have regained your realm, it is as though you must build it anew; to revive a ruined land demands redoubled effort. The Japanese may have withdrawn, but their people remain. Xing Jie is now ordered to bring the army home to the capital, while Wan Shide and others are to remain in designated strength as garrison troops. You must endure hardship and never forget this humiliation; through loyalty and filial piety, carry on the glory of your forebears. In the fifth month Xing Jie memorialized ten proposals for managing the aftermath of the eastern expedition. First, retain garrison forces: more than thirty-four thousand troops on land and sea, with three thousand horses. Second, set monthly pay at more than 918,000 taels of silver per year. Third, fix grain supplies: rice and beans totaling 130,000 piculs yearly, to be levied from Liaodong, Tianjin, Shandong, and other regions. Fourth, keep the central-route maritime defense intendant in post. Fifth, abolish the supply bureau. Sixth, strengthen the authority of field commanders. Seventh, add patrol forces. Eighth, divide coastal defense sectors. Ninth, institute regular military training. Tenth, require the Korean court itself to bear the costs. The court debated: "After years of strain the empire has only just caught its breath; we should strengthen our foundations at home rather than take on new burdens." Moreover, Korea after war and famine has suffered not only from the Japanese but also from the presence of our own armies. The proper course is to consult Korea first, assess whether their resources can sustain a garrison, and only then decide how many Ming troops should remain. Purchasing more horses, adding banner troops, creating patrol units, and appointing supply officials should all be halted. The Emperor ordered the grand coordinators and the Korean king to consult and report jointly. In the eighth month Seonjo sent tribute goods to support imperial construction projects and received the customary rewards in return. In the tenth month he asked that eight thousand naval troops be left behind for coastal defense. The troops being withdrawn were stationed at Liaoyang to stand ready against emergencies. In the fourth month of year twenty-eight he asked that surplus rice and beans in warehouses at Uiju and other places be shipped back to Liaoyang. The Ministry of Revenue advised: "The cost of transport is prohibitive; better to leave the grain in Korea to relieve their distress and display the Emperor’s mercy." The Emperor replied: "Let it be so."
55
二十九年二月，兵部覆奏經督條陳七事：「一，練兵士。 麗人鷙悍耐寒苦，而長衫大袖，訓練無方，宜以束伍之法教之。 一，守沖要。 朝鮮三面距海，釜山與對馬相望，巨濟次之，宜各守以重兵，並蔚山、開山等處皆宜戍守。 一，修險隘。 王京北倚叢山，南環滄海。 忠州左右烏、竹二嶺，羊腸繞曲，有一夫當關之險。 今營壘遺址尚存，亟宜修葺。 一，建城池。 朝鮮八道，十九無城。 平壤西北鴨、浿二江，俱南通海。 倘倭別遣一旅佔據平壤，則王京聲援斷絕，皆應修築屯聚。 一，造器械。 倭戰便陸不便海，以船制重大，不利攻擊。 今准福唬造百十艘為奇兵，並添造神機百子火箭。 一，訪異材。 朝鮮貴世官，賊世役，一切禁錮，往往走倭走敵，為本國患，宜破格搜采。 一，修內治。 國家東南臨海，以登、旅為門戶，鎮江為咽喉，應援之兵，不宜盡撤。 我自固，亦所以固朝鮮也。 」詔朝鮮刻勵以行。 九月，奏所頒誥命冕服遭變淪失，祈補給，從之。
In the second month of year twenty-nine the Ministry of War responded to seven proposals from the grand coordinator: "First, train the troops." Koreans are hardy and endure hardship well, but their long robes and wide sleeves reflect undisciplined training; they should be drilled using the squad-and-platoon system. Second, defend critical positions. Korea is surrounded by sea on three sides; Pusan, facing Tsushima, and Geoje, the next key harbor, each require strong garrisons, as do Ulsan, Gyeongju, and other vulnerable points. Third, fortify mountain defiles. Seoul rests against mountains to the north and is encircled by sea to the south. East and west of Chungju lie the Wu and Zhu ridges, where winding goat-tracks offer the classic chokepoint where a single defender can block an army. Remnants of old fortifications still stand there and should be restored without delay. Fourth, construct walled cities. Of Korea’s eight provinces, cities are absent in nineteen districts. Northwest of Pyongyang the Yalu and Taedong rivers both run south to the sea. If the Japanese landed a separate force at Pyongyang, Seoul would be isolated; fortifications and garrisons should be built accordingly. Fifth, produce arms and equipment. The Japanese fight well on land but poorly at sea; their vessels are built heavy and clumsy for offensive action. The court approved building more than a hundred swift warships as a strike force, along with additional divine-engine rocket batteries. Sixth, recruit men of exceptional ability. Korea’s hereditary aristocracy and bound labor service trap talent in rigid ranks, driving many to defect to Japan or to the enemy; officials should be recruited without regard to conventional restrictions. Seventh, strengthen domestic administration. The Ming southeastern coast faces the sea; Dengzhou and Lüshun are its gateway and Zhenjiang its throat; relief forces should not be fully withdrawn. By strengthening our own defenses we protect Korea as well. The court issued an edict instructing Korea to take these measures to heart and implement them. In the ninth month he reported that imperial patents, robes, and regalia had been lost in the war and asked for replacements; the court agreed.
56
時倭國內亂，對馬島主平義智悉遣降人還朝鮮，遺書乞和，且揚言秀吉將家康將輸糧數十萬石為軍興資，以脅朝鮮。 朝鮮與對馬島一水相望，島地不產五穀，資米於朝鮮。 兵興後，絕開市，因百計脅款。 秀吉死，我軍盡撤，朝鮮畏倭滋甚。 欲與倭通款，又懼開罪中國。 十二月，昖以島倭求款來請命。 兵部以事難遙度，令總督世德酌議，詔可。 三十年十一月，昖言倭使頻來要脅和款，兵端漸露，乞選將率兵，督同本國訓練修防。 帝曰：「曾留將士教習，成法具在，無容再遣。 因命其使臣齎敕誡勵。 三十三年九月，昖復請封琿為世子，禮部仍執立長之議。 三十五年四月，昖以家康求和來告，兵部議聽王自計而已。 由是和款不絕，後三年始畫開市之事。
Japan was then riven by civil disorder. The lord of Tsushima, So Yoshitoshi, returned all prisoners to Korea, sent a letter suing for peace, and threatened that Hideyoshi’s and Tokugawa Ieyasu’s forces would supply hundreds of thousands of piculs of grain to renew hostilities unless Korea complied. Korea and Tsushima are divided only by a narrow strait; the island grows no grain and depends on Korean rice. Trade had ceased with the outbreak of war, and the Japanese resorted to every form of coercion to reopen it. After Hideyoshi’s death the Ming armies withdrew entirely, and Korea’s fear of Japan only deepened. They wished to negotiate with Japan but feared offending the Ming. In the twelfth month Seonjo asked the court for guidance, reporting that the Japanese of Tsushima were seeking a negotiated peace. The Ministry of War, unable to judge the matter from a distance, ordered Wan Shide to decide on the spot; the Emperor assented. In the eleventh month of year thirty Seonjo reported that Japanese envoys were pressing repeatedly for peace talks while signs of renewed conflict appeared, and he asked that Ming generals be sent to train and fortify Korea alongside his own forces. The Emperor replied: "We have already left officers to train your forces, and the established procedures remain in place; we cannot send another mission." He instead had their envoys carry back an imperial edict of admonition and encouragement. In the ninth month of year thirty-three Seonjo again asked that Gwanghae be named heir apparent, but the Ministry of Rites still insisted on the rule of primogeniture. In the fourth month of year thirty-five Seonjo informed the court that Tokugawa Ieyasu was suing for peace; the Ministry of War decided to let the king manage the matter himself. Negotiations continued without a break, and trade was not formally reopened until three years later.
57
三十六年，昖卒。 光海君琿自稱署國事，追陪臣來訃，且請諡。 帝惡其擅，不允，令該國臣民公義以聞。 時我大清兵征服各部，漸近朝鮮。 兵部議令該王大修武備，整飭邊防，並請敕遼左督撫鎮臣，遣官宣達毋相侵犯之意。 從之。 十月，封琿為國王，從其臣民請也。 三十七年二月，諡昖曰昭敬，遣官賜琿及妃柳氏誥命。
In year thirty-six Seonjo died. Gwanghae-gun Hui declared himself regent, sent envoys to announce the death, and asked for a posthumous title for the late king. The Emperor disapproved of this presumption and refused consent, instructing Korea’s officials and people to decide the matter through public deliberation and report back. By then the armies of the rising Qing were subduing the Jurchen tribes and drawing ever nearer to Korea. The Ministry of War urged the Korean king to rebuild his defenses and tighten the frontier, and asked that eastern Liaodong officials be instructed to send envoys making clear that neither side should encroach on the other. The court approved. In the tenth month Gwanghae was invested as king, as his court and people had petitioned. In the second month of year thirty-seven Seonjo received the posthumous title Zhaojing, and envoys were sent to invest Gwanghae and his consort Lady Liu with imperial patents.
58
初，朝鮮失守，賴中國力得復，倭棄釜山遁。 然陰謀啟疆，為患不已。 於是海上流言倭圖釜山，朝鮮與之通。 四十一年九月，總兵官楊宗業以聞。 琿疏辨，詔慰解之。
When Korea had been overrun, it was only through Ming power that the kingdom was restored and the Japanese driven from Pusan. Yet Japan’s covert ambitions to expand its foothold brought unending trouble. Rumors then spread along the coast that Japan was plotting against Pusan and that Korea was colluding with them. In the ninth month of year forty-one Regional Commander Yang Zongye reported these rumors to the court. Gwanghae submitted a defense; the Emperor issued an edict reassuring him and dismissing the charge.
59
四十二年四月，奏請追封生母金氏。 禮部按《會典》，嫡母受封而生母先亡者得追贈，乃命封為國王次妃。 四十三年十一月，表賀冬至，因奏買回《吾學編》、《弇山堂別集》等書，載本國事與《會典》乖錯，乞改正。 禮部言：「野史不足憑。 今所請恥與逆黨同譏，宜憫其誠，宣付史館。 」報可。 初，琿為生母已得封，至是復祈給冠服。 禮臣以金氏側室，禮有隆殺，執不可。 四十五年正月，琿請至再，帝以琿屢次懇陳，勉從之。
In the fourth month of year forty-two he asked that his biological mother, Lady Jin, be granted posthumous rank. The Ministry of Rites, citing the 《Collected Statutes》, ruled that when the principal consort held rank and the birth mother was deceased, posthumous ennoblement was permitted, and Lady Jin was granted the title of the king’s secondary consort. In the eleventh month of year forty-three, in his winter-solstice tribute memorial, he also asked to purchase copies of 《Wuxue bian》, 《Yanshan tang bieji》, and other works that described Korean affairs in ways contradicting the 《Collected Statutes》, and requested that they be corrected. The Ministry of Rites replied: "Unofficial histories are not authoritative." Yet his request shows sincere distress at being lumped with rebels in those pages; the court should honor his earnestness and refer the matter to the Historiography Institute." The Emperor agreed. Gwanghae had already secured posthumous rank for his mother; now he asked again for ceremonial caps and robes. The ritual officials, noting that Lady Jin had been a concubine and that rites distinguish primary from secondary status, refused firmly. In the first month of year forty-five Gwanghae petitioned repeatedly; moved by his persistence, the Emperor at last yielded.
60
四十七年，楊鎬督馬林、杜松、劉綎等出師，為我大清兵所敗。 朝鮮助戰兵將，或降或戰死。 琿告急，詔加優恤。 十一月，兵部覆：朝鮮入貢之道，宜添兵防守。 詔鎮江等處設兵將，令經略熊廷弼調委。 四十八年正月，琿奏：「敵兵八月中攻破北關，金台吉自焚，白羊出降。 鐵嶺之役，蒙古宰賽亦為所滅。 聞其國謀議以朝鮮、北關、宰賽皆助兵南朝，今北關、宰賽皆滅，不可使朝鮮獨存。 又聞設兵牛毛寨、萬遮嶺，欲略寬奠、鎮江等處。 寬奠、鎮江與昌城、義州諸堡隔水相望，孤危非常。 敵若從靉陽境上鴉鶻關取路繞出鳳凰城裏，一日長驅，寬鎮、昌城俱莫自保。 內而遼左八站，外而東江一城，彼此隔斷，聲援阻絕，可為寒心。 望速調大兵，共為掎角，以固邊防。 」時遼鎮塘報稱朝鮮與大清講和，朝議遂謂琿陽衡陰順，宜遣官宣諭，或命將監護，其說紛拿。 琿疏辨：「二百年忠誠事大，死生一節。 」詞極剴摯。 禮、兵二部請降敕令曉諭，以安其心。 帝是其議，然敕令陪臣往，不遣官也。
In year forty-seven Grand Coordinator Yang Hao marched with Ma Lin, Du Song, Liu Ting, and others and was defeated by the Qing armies. Among the Korean troops who fought alongside them, some surrendered and others died in battle. Hui reported an emergency, and an edict granted additional generous relief. In the eleventh month the Ministry of War replied that additional troops should be posted to defend the route by which Korea presented tribute. An edict ordered commanders and troops posted at Jinjiang and other places, to be assigned and deployed by grand coordinator Xiong Tingbi. In the first month of the forty-eighth year Hui memorialized: "In the eighth month the enemy broke through the North Pass; Jin Taichi burned himself to death, and Baiyang surrendered. In the battle of Tieling the Mongol Zaisai was also destroyed by them. It was reported that their court was debating that Korea, the North Pass, and Zaisai had all sent troops to aid the Ming; now that the North Pass and Zaisai were both destroyed, Korea must not be allowed to stand alone. It was also reported that troops had been posted at Niumao Stockade and Wanzhe Ridge, intending to raid Gando, Jinjiang, and other places. Gando and Jinjiang faced Changseong, Uiju, and the other forts across the water and were extraordinarily isolated and imperiled. If the enemy took the route from Yaguguan on the Aiyang frontier and circled behind Fenghuangcheng, they could drive forward in a single day, and neither Gando-Jinjiang nor Changseong could be held. Within lay the eight Liaodong stations; without, the lone city of the Eastern River—all cut off from one another with mutual support blocked, enough to chill the heart. We beg that great forces be shifted quickly so that we may act in mutual support and secure the frontier defenses. " At that time Liaodong frontier reports stated that Korea had made peace with the Great Qing; court deliberation then held that Hui was outwardly resistant but secretly compliant, and that an envoy should be dispatched to instruct him or a general ordered to supervise—opinions were tangled and disputed. Hui submitted a memorial in rebuttal: "For two hundred years we have served the great power with loyal devotion, one integrity in life and death. " The language was extremely earnest and sincere. The Ministries of Rites and War requested that an imperial command be issued to instruct and reassure him. The emperor approved their proposal, yet the command was sent with Korean envoys and no official was dispatched.
61
天啟元年八月，改朝鮮貢道，自海至登州，直達京師。 時毛文龍以總兵鎮皮島，招集逃民為兵，而仰給於朝鮮。 十一月，琿奏力難饋餉，乞循萬曆東征例，發運山東粟，從之。 三年四月，國人廢琿而立其侄綾陽君倧，以昭敬王妃之命權國事，令議政府移文督撫轉奏，文龍為之揭報。 登州巡撫袁可立上言：「琿果不道，宜聽太妃具奏，以待中國更立。 」疏留中。 八月，王妃金氏疏請封倧，禮部尚書林堯俞言：「朝鮮廢立之事，內外諸臣抒忠發憤，有謂宜聲罪致討者，有謂勿遽討且受方貢核顛末者，或謂當責以大義，察輿情之向背者，或謂當令亻宗討敵自洗者，眾論鹹有可采。 其謂琿實悖德，倧討叛臣以赤心奉朝廷者，惟文龍一人耳。 皇上奉天討逆，扶植綱常，此正法也。 毋亦念彼素稱恭順，迥異諸裔，則更遣貞士信臣，會同文龍，公集臣民，再四詢訪。 勘辨既明，再請聖斷。 」報可。 十二月，禮部復上言：「臣前同兵部移咨登撫，並劄毛師，遣官往勘。 今據申送彼國公結十二道，自宗室至八道臣民共稱倧為恭順。 且彼之陪臣相率哀籲，謂當此危急之秋，必須君國之主。 乞先頒敕諭，令倧統理國事，仍令發兵索賦，同文龍設伏出奇，俟漸有次第，始遣重臣往正封典。 庶幾字小之中，不失固圉之道。 」從之。 四年四月，封倧為國王。
In the eighth month of the first year of Tianqi the Korean tribute route was changed to run from the sea to Dengzhou and then straight to the capital. At that time regional commander Mao Wenlong garrisoned Pidao, gathering fugitive civilians as troops and relying on Korea for supplies. In the eleventh month Hui memorialized that he could scarcely sustain provisions and requested that, following the precedent of the Wanli eastern campaign, grain be shipped from Shandong; approval was granted. In the fourth month of the third year the people deposed Hui and enthroned his nephew Ryangyanggun Jeong, who by order of Queen Dowager Zhaojing provisionally managed state affairs; the Council of State was ordered to send a dispatch to the grand coordinators for relay to the throne, and Wenlong reported it in a memorial. Dengzhou grand coordinator Yuan Keli submitted: "If Hui is indeed without the Way, the queen dowager should be allowed to submit a full memorial and await reestablishment by China. The memorial was held at court. In the eighth month Queen Consort Lady Jin submitted a memorial requesting investiture for Jeong; Minister of Rites Lin Yaoyu said: "On Korea's deposition and enthronement, officials within and without have poured forth loyal indignation: some say we should proclaim guilt and launch punitive action; some say we should not hasten to punish but accept their tribute and verify the facts; some say we should charge them with the great principle and observe where popular sentiment inclines; some say Jeong should be ordered to campaign against the enemy to clear himself—all these views have points worth adopting. Of those who say Hui was truly devoid of virtue and that Jeong suppressed rebels with a loyal heart in service to the court, Wenlong alone is such a man. Your Majesty, following Heaven, punishes rebellion and upholds the moral order—this is the correct law. Yet also consider that they have long been called respectful and compliant, utterly unlike other border peoples—then dispatch upright and trustworthy officials, together with Wenlong, to assemble officials and people openly and inquire repeatedly. Once investigation and judgment are clear, then request the sacred decision again. Approval was granted. In the twelfth month the Ministry of Rites again submitted: "Your servant previously jointly with the Ministry of War sent instructions to the Dengzhou grand coordinator and also wrote to Commander Mao, dispatching officials to investigate. Now according to the twelve jointly signed documents submitted from that state, from the royal house to the officials and people of the eight provinces, all call Jeong respectful and compliant. Moreover their envoys have one after another pleaded in grief, saying that in this hour of critical peril a ruler who can govern the state is essential. They beg that an edict of instruction be issued first, ordering Jeong to administer state affairs and also ordering the dispatch of troops and collection of levies, together with Wenlong setting ambushes and striking with surprise; when matters gradually take order, then send a high official to confer the proper investiture. Thus perhaps within the care shown to a small state the way of securing the frontier will not be lost. Approval was granted. In the fourth month of the fourth year Jeong was invested as king.
62
五年十二月，文龍報：「朝鮮逆党李適、韓明璉等起兵昌城，直趨王京，被臣擒獲。 餘孽韓潤、鄭梅等竄入建州，有左議府尹義立約為內應，期今冬大舉犯朝鮮。 臣已咨國王防守，暫移鐵山之眾就雲從島柴薪。 」登萊巡撫武之望奏：「毛帥自五月以來，營室於須彌，所謂雲從島是也。 今十月又徙兵民商賈以實之，而鐵山之地空矣。 故朝鮮各道疑其有逼處之嫌，甚至布兵以防禦之。 今鎮臣所稱李適等之叛，尹義立之內應，臣等微聞之，而未敢遽信焉。 信之則益重鮮人之疑，不信則恐貽後來之患。 」兵部言：「牽制敵國者，朝鮮也； 聯屬朝鮮者，毛鎮也； 駕馭毛鎮者，登撫也。 今撫臣與鎮臣不和，以至鎮臣與屬國不和，大不利。 」帝乃飭勉鎮撫同心，而韓潤、尹義立等令朝鮮自處。 倧又請撤遼民安插中土，兵部言：「遼人去留，文龍是視。 文龍一日不去，則遼人一日不離。 鮮人驅之入島可也，驅之離島不可也。 宜令鎮臣將遼民盡刷過島，登撫刻期運糧朝鮮，量行救振，以資屯牧。 」帝是之。
In the twelfth month of the fifth year Wenlong reported: "The Korean rebel faction Li Shi, Han Minglian, and others raised troops at Changseong and marched straight on the royal capital; they were captured by your servant. The remaining ringleaders Han Run, Zheng Mei, and others fled into Jianzhou; Left State Councilor Yin Yili arranged to serve as internal collaborators, planning a major invasion of Korea this winter. Your servant has already consulted the king on defense and temporarily moved the forces at Tieshan to gather firewood at Yundao Island. The Deng-Lai grand coordinator Wu Zhiwang memorialized: "Since the fifth month Commander Mao has built quarters at Sumi—what is called Yundao Island. Now in the tenth month he has again moved troops, civilians, and merchants to fill it, and the land at Tieshan is empty. Therefore the various Korean provinces suspect there is cause for concern over encroachment, and some have even deployed troops in defense. What the regional commander reports of the rebellion of Li Shi and the internal collusion of Yin Yili, your servants have faintly heard of it but did not dare hastily to believe it. If we believe it, we will only deepen Korean suspicions; if we do not believe it, we may leave trouble for the future. The Ministry of War said: "The one who checks the enemy state is Korea; the one who links Korea is the Mao garrison; the one who controls the Mao garrison is the Dengzhou grand coordinator. Now the grand coordinator and the regional commander are at odds, to the point that the regional commander is at odds with the tributary state—this is greatly unfavorable. The emperor then admonished the regional and grand coordinators to act in concert, and left Han Run, Yin Yili, and the others for Korea to handle itself. Jeong also requested the removal of Liaodong civilians settled in the interior; the Ministry of War said: "Whether Liaodong people stay or go depends on Wenlong. As long as Wenlong does not leave, the Liaodong people will not depart. It is acceptable for Koreans to drive them onto the island; it is not acceptable to drive them off the island. The regional commander should be ordered to move all Liaodong civilians onto the island; the Dengzhou grand coordinator should set a deadline to transport grain to Korea and provide relief as appropriate to support garrison farming. The emperor approved.
63
六年十月，倧上疏曰：
In the tenth month of the sixth year Jeong submitted a memorial saying:
64
皇朝之於小邦，覆幬之恩，視同服內。 頃遭昏亂，潛通敵國，皇天震怒，降黜厥命。 臣自權署之初，不敢遑寧，即命陪臣張晚為帥，李適副之，付以國中精銳，進屯甯邊，一聽毛鎮節制，以候協剿之期。 而適重兵在握，潛蓄覬覦，遂與龜城府使明璉舉兵內叛，直犯京城。 晚收餘兵躡其後，與京輔官兵表裏夾攻，賊皆授首，而西邊軍實及列鎮儲偫罄於是役矣。
The august court's kindness toward our small state shelters us as if we were within the inner domain. Recently we suffered disorder and secretly communicated with the enemy state; Heaven was angered and deposed our mandate. From the beginning of my provisional administration I have not dared rest; I immediately appointed envoy Zhang Wan as commander and Li Shi as his deputy, giving them the elite forces of the state and advancing to encamp at Pyeongan, entirely under Commander Mao's direction, to await the time for joint suppression. But Shi, with heavy troops in hand, secretly harbored ambition, and together with Gyeongju prefect Han Minglian raised troops in internal rebellion and marched straight on the capital. Wan gathered the remaining troops and followed behind, and with the capital garrison acting in concert from within and without, the rebels were all beheaded; yet the military strength of the western frontier and the stored provisions of the garrison districts were exhausted in this campaign.
65
毛鎮當全遼淪沒之後，孤軍東渡，寄寓海上，招集遼民前後數十萬，亦小邦所仰藉也。 顧以封疆多故，土瘠民貧，內供本國之軍需，外濟鎮兵之待哺，生谷有限，支給實難。 遼民迫於饑餒，散佈村落，強者攫奪，弱者丐乞。 小邦兵民被撓不堪，拋棄鄉邑，轉徙內地。 遼民逐食，亦隨而入。 自昌、義以南，安、肅以北，客居六七，主居三四。 向者將此情形具奏，見兵部題覆處分已定，何敢再幹。
Commander Mao, after all of Liaodong had fallen, crossed east alone with a solitary army, dwelling on the sea and gathering Liaodong civilians numbering several hundred thousand in all—our small state also relies on him. Yet with the borders in constant turmoil, the soil poor and the people impoverished, supplying our own state's military needs within and sustaining the garrison troops' rations without—the living grain is limited, and support is truly difficult. Liaodong people, pressed by hunger, scattered through the villages; the strong seized by force, the weak begged for food. Our small state's soldiers and civilians, harassed beyond endurance, abandoned their villages and moved into the interior. Liaodong people seeking food followed them in as well. From Chang and Ui southward and An and Suk northward, guests occupy six or seven parts and hosts three or four. Previously I reported this situation in full; once the Ministry of War had replied with its disposition settled, how could I dare raise it again.
66
至韓潤及弟潭系逆賊明璉子侄，亡命潛逃，因而勾引來寇。 賊既叛國而去，制命已不在臣。 尹義立曾任判書，本非議政。 頃年差為毛鎮接伴官，不稱任使，褫職歸家，並無怨叛之事。 毛鎮據王仲保等所訴，都無實事。 意必有讒邪之臣，欺妄督撫，以售其交構之計者。
As for Han Run and his younger brother Tan, they are the sons and nephews of the rebel Minglian; they fled as outlaws and in flight drew the enemy to invade. Once the rebels had betrayed the state and fled, command over them was no longer in my hands. Yin Yili once served as minister of the board; he was never a chief councilor. In recent years he was assigned as Commander Mao's reception officer; he did not fulfill his duties, was stripped of office and returned home, and there was no matter of resentment or rebellion. Commander Mao, relying on the complaints of Wang Zhongbao and others, found no substantiating facts at all. I suspect there are slanderous ministers who deceived the grand coordinator and sold their scheme of sowing discord.
67
毛帥久鎮海外，臣與周旋已近十稔。 雖餼牽將竭，彼此俱困，而情誼之殷，實無少損。 且其須彌之遷，直為保護累重，將以就便芻薪。 一進一退，兵家常事。 訛言噂遝，本不介意。 竊見部撫移咨曰「虞其逼處」，曰「驅其民，驅其帥」，甚至有「布兵以防，屬國攜貳」之語，似海外情事，未盡諒悉。 臣之請刷遼民，因力不足濟，初非慮及逼處也。 臣方與毛鎮同心一力，建功報主，豈敢有一毫猜防意乎。
Commander Mao has long garrisoned beyond the sea; I have dealt with him for nearly ten years. Although provisions are nearly exhausted and both sides are equally distressed, the warmth of our bond has truly not diminished in the least. Moreover his move to Sumi was directly to protect his heavy encumbrance and to obtain fodder and firewood conveniently. Advancing and retreating are common matters in warfare. Rumors and gossip I originally did not take to heart. I have seen the ministry and grand coordinator's dispatch say "fear encroachment," say "drive out their people, drive out their commander," and even language of "deploying troops in defense, the tributary state turning disloyal"—it seems affairs beyond the sea have not been fully understood. My request to relocate Liaodong civilians arose because my strength was insufficient to sustain them; it was not originally from fear of encroachment. I am now of one mind with Commander Mao, striving together to achieve merit and repay our lord—how could I dare harbor the slightest suspicion.
68
帝報曰：「王和協東鎮，愛戴中朝，忠貞之忱，溢乎言表。 鎮軍久懸，鮮、遼雜處。 久客累主，生寡食多。 微王言，朕有不坐照萬里之外者。 然毛帥在中朝為牽制之師，在王國則脣齒之形也。 海上芻輓，已令該部區畫，刻期運濟。 逃難邊民，亦令毛帥悉心計處，俾無重為王累。 傳訛之言，未足介懷，並力一心，王其勉之。」
The emperor replied: "The king harmonizes with the eastern garrison and cherishes the central court; loyal devotion overflows in your words. The garrison army has long been suspended; Koreans and Liaodong people are mixed together. Long-staying guests burden their host; the living are few and the mouths to feed are many. But for the king's words, there are matters ten thousand li away of which We would not have been fully informed. Yet Commander Mao, within China, is a force that checks the enemy; within the king's realm he is lip and teeth. Transport of fodder by sea has already been ordered to the relevant ministry for planning, with a fixed deadline for delivery. Refugee border people are also ordered to be fully arranged by Commander Mao so that they will not again heavily burden the king. Transmitted rumors are not worth taking to heart; exert your strength as one—let the king strive on."
69
七年三月，兵部上文龍揭言：「麗官、麗人招敵攻鐵山，傷我兵千人，殺麗兵六萬，焚糧百余萬，敵遂移兵攻麗矣。 」帝敕文龍速相機應援。 登撫李嵩奏：「朝鮮叛臣韓潤等引敵入安州，節度使南以興自焚死，中國援兵都司王三桂等俱陣亡。 」既復奏：「義州及郭山、淩漢、山城俱破，平壤、黃州不戰自潰，敵兵直抵中和，游騎出入黃、鳳之間，又分向雲從，攻掠毛帥，國王及士民遷于江華以避難。 」時大清兵所至輒下，朝鮮列城望風奔潰，乃遣使諭倧。 倧輸款，遂班師。 九月，倧奏被兵情形。 時熹宗崩，莊烈帝嗣位，優詔勵勉焉。
In the third month of the seventh year the Ministry of War submitted Wenlong's memorial stating: "Korean officials and Korean people lured the enemy to attack Tieshan, wounding a thousand of our troops, killing sixty thousand Korean troops, and burning more than a million units of grain; the enemy then shifted troops to attack Korea. The emperor commanded Wenlong to respond swiftly as circumstances allowed. Grand coordinator Li Song memorialized: "The Korean rebel minister Han Run and others led the enemy into Anzhou; military governor Nam Yixing burned himself to death, and Chinese relief commanders including Metropolitan Commissioner Wang Sanguai all died in battle. He memorialized again: "Uiju and Guoshan, Linghan, and the mountain fortress were all taken; Pyongyang and Hwangju collapsed without battle; enemy troops reached directly to Junghwa, raiding cavalry ranged between Hwang and Pung, and detachments also turned toward Yundao to attack and plunder Commander Mao; the king and officials and people moved to Ganghwa to escape the calamity. At that time wherever the Great Qing troops arrived they took cities; Korean walled towns fled and collapsed at the wind; they then dispatched envoys to instruct Jeong. Jeong submitted terms of surrender, and they then withdrew the army. In the ninth month Jeong memorialized on the circumstances of suffering attack. At that time Emperor Xizong died and Emperor Sizong succeeded; an edict of special favor encouraged and exhorted him.
70
崇禎二年，改每歲兩貢為一貢。 先是，遼路阻絕，貢使取道登、萊，已十餘年矣。 自袁崇煥督師，題改覺華，迂途冒險，其國屢請復故。 至是遣戶曹判書鄭鬥源從登海來，移書登撫孫元化，屬其陳請。 元化委官伴送，仍疏聞。 帝以水路既有成命，改途嫌於自便，不許。 是年六月，督師袁崇煥殺平遼將軍左都督毛文龍於雙島。 六年六月，倧遺書總兵黃龍言：「文龍舊將孔有德、耿仲明率士卒二萬投順大清，向朝鮮征糧。 本國以有德等曩在皮島為本國患，故未之應。 」龍以聞。 十年正月，太宗文皇帝親征朝鮮，責其渝盟助明之罪，列城悉潰。 朝鮮告急，命總兵陳洪范調各鎮舟師赴援。 三月，洪范奏官兵出海。 越數日，山東巡撫顏繼祖奏屬國失守，江華已破，世子被擒，國王出降。 今大治舟艦，來攻皮島、鐵山，其鋒甚銳。 宜急敕沈世魁、陳洪範二鎮臣，以堅守皮島為第一義。 帝以繼祖不能協圖匡救，切責之。 亡何，皮島並為大清兵所破，朝鮮遂絕，不數載而明亦亡矣。 朝鮮在明雖稱屬國，而無異域內。 故朝貢絡繹，錫賚便蕃，殆不勝書，止著其有關治亂者於篇。 至國之風土物產，則具載前史，茲不復錄。
In the second year of Chongzhen the annual two tribute missions were changed to one. Previously the Liaodong route had been cut off, and tribute envoys had taken the route through Deng and Lai for more than ten years already. When Yuan Chonghuan served as supreme commander he proposed changing to Juehua, a roundabout route full of peril; their state repeatedly requested restoration of the former route. At this time Minister of Revenue Zheng Douyuan came from the Deng-Hai route and sent a letter to grand coordinator Sun Yuanhua, asking him to submit the request on their behalf. Yuanhua delegated officials to escort them and memorialized the court. The emperor held that since the water route already had a fixed arrangement, changing routes seemed self-serving and was not permitted. That year in the sixth month supreme commander Yuan Chonghuan executed Mao Wenlong, pacification general of Liaodong and left censor-in-chief, at Shuangdao. In the sixth year, sixth month, King Jong sent a letter to regional commander Huang Long, stating, "Mao Wenlong's former subordinates Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming have led twenty thousand troops in submission to the Great Qing and come to Korea to requisition grain. Our state, because Youde and the others had formerly been a scourge to us while at Pidao, did not comply. Huang Long reported the matter. In the tenth year, first month, Taizong the Literary Emperor personally campaigned against Korea, charging it with breaking the alliance and aiding Ming, and walled cities collapsed one after another. Korea reported in urgent distress, and regional commander Chen Hongfan was ordered to mobilize naval forces from the various garrisons to go to their aid. In the third month Hongfan memorialized that government troops had put to sea. Several days later Shandong grand coordinator Yan Jizu memorialized that the tributary state had fallen, Ganghwa was already taken, the heir apparent had been captured, and the king had surrendered. Now they are building warships in great numbers and coming to attack Pidao and Jeoksan, and their momentum is very sharp. Shen Shikui and Chen Hongfan, the two garrison commanders, should be urgently ordered to make holding Pidao their first priority. The emperor, holding that Jizu had failed to cooperate in planning a rescue, sharply rebuked him. Before long Pidao was also overrun by Great Qing troops; contact with Korea then ceased, and within a few years Ming perished as well. Korea in Ming times, though called a tributary state, was in practice no different from territory within the realm. Tribute missions therefore came in unbroken succession and imperial gifts were too frequent to record in full; this chapter records only those matters bearing on order and disorder. As for the state's customs and local products, the earlier histories record them fully, and they are not repeated here.
